lion.name: Lion
descriptions: Only cat species that lives in social groups called prides
A lion's roar can be heard up to 8 km away
Females do most of the hunting, usually at night
Males can weigh up to 250 kg
Sleeps up to 20 hours a day

tigre.name: Tiger
descriptions: Largest of all wild cat species
Each tiger has a unique pattern of stripes
Can eat up to 40 kg of meat in one sitting
Excellent swimmers that enjoy bathing in rivers
Fewer than 4,000 remain in the wild

leopard.name: Leopard
descriptions: Can carry prey twice its weight up a tree
Most widespread of all big cats
Excellent nocturnal hunter with superb night vision
Rosette-shaped spots help it blend into foliage
Can run at speeds up to 58 km/h

jaguar.name: Jaguar
descriptions: Has the strongest bite of all big cats
Spots are called rosettes with a central dot
Loves water and is an excellent swimmer
Can crush a turtle shell with its jaws
Third largest cat in the world

panthere-des-neiges.name: Snow leopard
descriptions: Lives at altitudes above 3,000 meters
Tail is nearly as long as its body for balance
Cannot roar, unlike other big cats
Paws act as natural snowshoes
Can leap up to 15 meters in a single bound

guepard.name: Cheetah
descriptions: Fastest land animal, reaching 112 km/h
Accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in 3 seconds
Has semi-retractable claws like running spikes
Black tear marks reduce sun glare while hunting
Cannot roar but can purr like a house cat

puma.name: Cougar
descriptions: Holds the Guinness record for most names of any animal
Can leap 5.5 meters vertically from standing
Found from Canada to the tip of South America
Cannot roar but produces a piercing scream
Also known as cougar, mountain lion, or panther

lynx-boreal.name: Eurasian lynx
descriptions: Largest lynx species, weighing up to 30 kg
Ear tufts help direct sound to its ears
Can spot a mouse at 75 meters away
Lives in dense forests across Europe and Asia
Paws spread wide to act as snowshoes

lynx-iberique.name: Iberian lynx
descriptions: World's most endangered cat species
Found only on the Iberian Peninsula
Feeds almost exclusively on rabbits
Distinctive beard-like facial ruff
Population recovered from under 100 to over 1,000

ocelot.name: Ocelot
descriptions: Salvador Dali kept an ocelot as a pet
Sleeps in trees during the day
Each ocelot has a unique coat pattern
Swims well and hunts fish and crabs
Also called the painted leopard

serval.name: Serval
descriptions: Has the longest legs relative to body of any cat
Can leap 3 meters high to catch birds mid-flight
Hunting success rate of around 50 percent
Ears are the largest relative to body of any cat
Lives in African savannas and wetlands

caracal.name: Caracal
descriptions: Can swat birds out of the air with its paws
Name comes from Turkish for 'black ear'
Ear tufts are over 4 cm long
Can jump 3 meters high from a standstill
Was trained for bird hunting in ancient Persia

chat-sauvage.name: European wildcat
descriptions: Ancestor of all domestic cats
Looks like a tabby but is larger and stockier
Extremely shy and avoids humans
Lives in forests across Europe and Asia
Tail is thick with a rounded black tip

leopard-des-neiges.name: Clouded leopard
descriptions: Known as the ghost of the mountains
Thick tail stores fat for harsh winters
Can survive at altitudes up to 5,500 meters
Fewer than 7,000 remain in the wild
Hunts prey up to three times its own weight

chat-de-pallas.name: Pallas's cat
descriptions: Has round pupils unlike most small cats
Fur is the longest and densest of any cat
Lives on the cold steppes of Central Asia
Also called the manul
Flat face helps it peer over rocks while hiding

loup-gris.name: Gray wolf
descriptions: Lives in packs with a strict social hierarchy
Can travel up to 70 km in a single day
Howl can be heard up to 16 km away
Ancestor of all domestic dog breeds
Can eat up to 9 kg of meat in one meal

renard-roux.name: Red fox
descriptions: Most widespread wild carnivore on Earth
Uses Earth's magnetic field to hunt in snow
Can hear a watch ticking 40 meters away
Found on every continent except Antarctica
Bushy tail helps with balance and warmth

renard-polaire.name: Arctic fox
descriptions: Fur changes from white in winter to brown in summer
Survives temperatures as low as minus 70 degrees C
Thick tail wraps around its body like a blanket
Has fur on the soles of its feet for grip on ice
Can locate prey under a meter of snow by sound

fennec.name: Fennec fox
descriptions: Smallest fox species in the world
Enormous ears radiate heat to keep it cool
Can go indefinitely without drinking water
Digs burrows up to 10 meters long in desert sand
Nocturnal to avoid the Sahara's extreme heat

lycaon.name: African wild dog
descriptions: Most successful predator in Africa at 80 percent
Hunts in cooperative packs of up to 30
Each individual has a unique coat pattern
Feeds sick and injured members of the pack
Also called the African painted dog

coyote.name: Coyote
descriptions: Has expanded its range despite human development
Can run at speeds up to 65 km/h
Mates for life and both parents raise pups
One of few large predators thriving in cities
Name comes from the Aztec word coyotl

chacal-dore.name: Golden jackal
descriptions: Most widespread jackal species
Mates for life and pairs hunt together
Expanding rapidly across Europe
Highly adaptable omnivore
Can run at speeds up to 50 km/h

dhole.name: Dhole
descriptions: Asian wild dog that hunts in packs of 5 to 12
Can bring down prey ten times its size
Communicates with whistles rather than howls
Endangered with fewer than 2,500 adults left
Found in forests from India to Southeast Asia

loup-a-criniere.name: Maned wolf
descriptions: Tallest wild canid in the world
Not a true wolf despite its name
Long legs help it see over tall grasslands
Urine smells like cannabis due to a chemical compound
Eats a lot of fruit, especially wolf apples

ours-brun.name: Brown bear
descriptions: Can weigh over 600 kg before hibernation
Runs at up to 56 km/h despite its size
Has a stronger bite than a great white shark
Eats up to 40 kg of food per day in autumn
Cubs stay with their mother for 2 to 3 years

ours-polaire.name: Polar bear
descriptions: Largest land carnivore on Earth
Fur appears white but each hair is transparent
Skin underneath its fur is actually black
Can swim continuously for over 100 km
Relies on sea ice to hunt seals

panda-geant.name: Giant panda
descriptions: Eats bamboo for up to 14 hours a day
Has a pseudo-thumb to grip bamboo stalks
Newborns are 900 times smaller than their mother
One of the rarest bears in the world
Symbol of the World Wildlife Fund since 1961

ours-noir-americain.name: American black bear
descriptions: Most common bear in North America
Excellent tree climber even as an adult
Can run at speeds up to 55 km/h
Not always black; can be brown, cinnamon, or blond
Heart rate drops to 8 beats per minute in winter

ours-a-lunettes.name: Spectacled bear
descriptions: Only bear species in South America
Named for markings that look like spectacles
Builds tree platforms to sleep and eat in
Inspired the story of Paddington Bear
Mainly herbivorous, eating bromeliads and fruit

ours-malais.name: Sun bear
descriptions: Smallest bear species in the world
Has the longest tongue of any bear at 25 cm
Uses long claws to open tree trunks for honey
Also known as the sun bear
Lives in tropical forests of Southeast Asia

ours-lippu.name: Sloth bear
descriptions: Sucks up insects with its flexible lips like a vacuum
Can hang upside down from branches like a sloth
Long shaggy fur makes it look bigger than it is
Carries cubs on its back for up to 9 months
Also known as the sloth bear

loutre-d-europe.name: European otter
descriptions: Can hold its breath for up to 4 minutes
Waterproof fur has up to 80,000 hairs per sq cm
Closes ears and nostrils when diving
Eats about 1 kg of fish per day
Playful behavior includes sliding down muddy banks

loutre-de-mer.name: Sea otter
descriptions: Uses rocks as tools to crack open shellfish
Has the densest fur of any mammal
Sleeps floating on its back in kelp forests
Holds hands with other otters to avoid drifting
Eats 25 percent of its body weight daily

hermine.name: Stoat
descriptions: Fur turns completely white in winter
Can kill prey much larger than itself
Performs a hypnotic dance to confuse prey
White winter coat was used for royal robes
One of the smallest carnivores in the world

belette.name: Least weasel
descriptions: Smallest carnivore in the world
Can fit through any hole its head can enter
Heart beats up to 400 times per minute
Must eat a third of its body weight daily
Bold enough to attack prey ten times its size

blaireau-europeen.name: European badger
descriptions: Lives in underground sett systems for generations
Setts can have over 50 entrances
Keeps its burrow extremely clean
Omnivore that especially loves earthworms
Sleeps through most of winter but is not a true hibernator

glouton.name: Wolverine
descriptions: Pound for pound the strongest mammalian predator
Can crush frozen meat and bone with its jaws
Roams territories up to 1,500 square km
Largest member of the weasel family
Also known as the wolverine

ratel.name: Honey badger
descriptions: Often called the world's most fearless animal
Thick rubbery skin resists bee stings and bites
Can escape from almost any enclosure
Eats venomous snakes and is resistant to venom
Also known as the honey badger

martre-des-pins.name: European pine marten
descriptions: Agile tree climber that can run down squirrels
Has a distinctive creamy yellow throat patch
Mainly active at dawn and dusk
Omnivore that also eats berries and fruit
Lives in dense coniferous and mixed forests

vison-d-europe.name: European mink
descriptions: One of the most endangered mammals in Europe
Excellent swimmer with partially webbed feet
Always has a white patch on its upper lip
Hunts fish, frogs, and small mammals near water
Threatened by the invasive American mink

hyene-tachetee.name: Spotted hyena
descriptions: Has the strongest bite of any mammal its size
Females are larger and dominant over males
Hunts in coordinated packs of up to 80
Laugh-like call can be heard 5 km away
Can digest bones, hooves, and even teeth

suricate.name: Meerkat
descriptions: Stands upright as a sentry to watch for predators
Lives in groups of up to 50 called mobs
Dark patches around eyes reduce sun glare
Teaches young how to eat scorpions safely
Found in the Kalahari Desert of southern Africa

mangouste-rayee.name: Banded mongoose
descriptions: Immune to some types of snake venom
Lives in social groups of up to 40 individuals
Distinctive dark stripes on its back
Cooperates to fight off predators like eagles
Found in eastern and southern Africa

fossa.name: Fossa
descriptions: Largest predator on the island of Madagascar
Looks like a cross between a cat and a mongoose
Can climb trees headfirst both up and down
Hunts lemurs through the forest canopy
Closely related to the mongoose family

panda-roux.name: Red panda
descriptions: Was called panda 50 years before the giant panda
Spends most of its life in trees
Uses its bushy tail as a blanket in cold weather
Mainly eats bamboo like the giant panda
Has a false thumb to grip bamboo

raton-laveur.name: Common raccoon
descriptions: Washes its food in water before eating
Front paws are incredibly dexterous like hands
Black face mask reduces glare for night vision
Can remember solutions to tasks for three years
Native to North America but invasive in Europe

coati-roux.name: South American coati
descriptions: Long flexible snout helps it forage for insects
Females live in bands of up to 30 individuals
Can rotate its ankles 180 degrees to descend trees
Tail is held upright while walking in groups
Related to raccoons but has a longer nose

phoque-gris.name: Grey seal
descriptions: Largest breeding seal in the North Atlantic
Males can weigh up to 300 kg
Pups are born with white fluffy fur
Can dive to depths of over 300 meters
Lives for up to 35 years in the wild

phoque-commun.name: Harbor seal
descriptions: Most widespread pinniped in the world
Can sleep in water in a position called bottling
Whiskers detect vibrations from fish underwater
Pups can swim within hours of birth
Lives along coastlines of the Northern Hemisphere

elephant-de-mer-du-sud.name: Southern elephant seal
descriptions: Largest seal species, males weigh up to 4,000 kg
Can dive deeper than 2,000 meters
Males have a huge inflatable nose trunk
Spends 80 percent of its life underwater
Males fight fierce battles for breeding rights

phoque-moine-de-mediterranee.name: Mediterranean monk seal
descriptions: One of the world's most endangered marine mammals
Fewer than 700 individuals remain
Lives in caves along the Mediterranean coast
Can hold its breath for up to 15 minutes
Named because its folds of skin resemble a monk's hood

otarie-a-fourrure.name: Cape fur seal
descriptions: Has both an underfur and guard hairs for insulation
Can walk on all four flippers on land
Males are up to five times heavier than females
Hunted nearly to extinction for its dense fur
Breeds in huge colonies of thousands

lion-de-mer-de-californie.name: California sea lion
descriptions: The classic performing seal in circuses and shows
Can swim at speeds up to 40 km/h
Males bark loudly to defend territory
Highly intelligent and easily trained
Can dive to depths over 270 meters

morse.name: Walrus
descriptions: Tusks can grow up to one meter long
Uses tusks to haul itself onto ice floes
Has up to 700 sensitive whiskers called vibrissae
Can slow its heartbeat to endure cold water
Lives in large herds on Arctic ice

baleine-bleue.name: Blue whale
descriptions: Largest animal ever to have lived on Earth
Heart is the size of a small car
Tongue alone weighs as much as an elephant
Can eat 4 tonnes of krill per day
Call can be detected over 1,600 km away

baleine-a-bosse.name: Humpback whale
descriptions: Males sing complex songs lasting up to 20 minutes
Migrates up to 8,000 km each season
Uses bubble nets to trap schools of fish
Pectoral fins can be 5 meters long
Known for breaching displays

rorqual-commun.name: Fin whale
descriptions: Second largest animal ever to live on Earth
Can reach speeds of 37 km/h, the fastest large whale
Asymmetrical coloring: right jaw is white, left is dark
Consumes up to 2 tonnes of food per day
Can grow up to 27 meters long

baleine-franche.name: North Atlantic right whale
descriptions: Named by whalers as the 'right' whale to hunt
No dorsal fin, unlike most other whales
Callosities on its head are unique like fingerprints
One of the most endangered large whales
Can live over 100 years

cachalot.name: Sperm whale
descriptions: Has the largest brain of any animal ever
Can dive over 2,000 meters deep
Hunts giant squid in the deep ocean
Inspired Herman Melville's novel Moby Dick
Makes the loudest sound of any animal at 230 decibels

orque.name: Orca
descriptions: Top predator of the ocean with no natural enemies
Lives in matriarchal family pods
Each pod has its own unique dialect of calls
Can swim at speeds up to 56 km/h
Hunts cooperatively using complex strategies

grand-dauphin.name: Common bottlenose dolphin
descriptions: Recognizes itself in a mirror, showing self-awareness
Sleeps with one eye open and half its brain awake
Can swim at speeds up to 35 km/h
Uses echolocation to find prey in murky water
Has been observed using sponges as tools

dauphin-commun.name: Common dolphin
descriptions: Can form super-pods of over 10,000 individuals
Leaps high out of the water while traveling
Found in temperate and tropical oceans worldwide
One of the fastest marine mammals at 60 km/h
Has up to 240 small sharp teeth

beluga.name: Beluga whale
descriptions: Known as the canary of the sea for its vocalizations
Can turn its head unlike most other whales
Born grey or brown and turns white with age
Has a flexible melon-shaped forehead for echolocation
Lives in Arctic and sub-Arctic waters

narval.name: Narwhal
descriptions: Long spiral tusk is actually an elongated tooth
Tusk can grow up to 3 meters long
Known as the unicorn of the sea
Tusk contains millions of nerve endings
Lives year-round in Arctic waters

marsouin-commun.name: Harbor porpoise
descriptions: One of the smallest cetaceans at about 1.5 meters
Rarely jumps out of the water unlike dolphins
Has spade-shaped teeth unlike conical dolphin teeth
Can dive to 200 meters and hold breath 6 minutes
Found in coastal waters of the Northern Hemisphere

vaquita.name: Vaquita
descriptions: World's most endangered marine mammal
Fewer than 10 individuals remain
Found only in Mexico's Gulf of California
Smallest porpoise species at about 1.4 meters
Dark rings around eyes and lips give a sad look

gorille-des-montagnes.name: Mountain gorilla
descriptions: Shares 98 percent of its DNA with humans
Males develop silver hair on backs with age
Lives only in the mountains of central Africa
About 1,000 individuals remain in the wild
Gentle herbivore that rarely shows aggression

gorille-des-plaines.name: Western lowland gorilla
descriptions: Most numerous gorilla subspecies
Males can weigh up to 200 kg
Beats its chest to communicate and show dominance
Builds a new sleeping nest every night
Lives in the tropical forests of West Africa

chimpanze.name: Chimpanzee
descriptions: Closest living relative to humans at 98.7 percent DNA
Uses tools such as sticks to extract termites
Can learn sign language and symbols
Lives in complex social groups of up to 150
One of the few animals that wages war on rivals

bonobo.name: Bonobo
descriptions: Resolves conflicts through social bonding not fighting
Led by females, unlike chimpanzees
Found only south of the Congo River
Shares food with strangers, a rare animal trait
Can walk upright more easily than chimpanzees

orang-outan-de-borneo.name: Bornean orangutan
descriptions: Most solitary of the great apes
Builds elaborate sleeping nests in trees each night
Males develop large cheek pads called flanges
Has the longest childhood of any primate: 8 years
Critically endangered due to deforestation

orang-outan-de-sumatra.name: Sumatran orangutan
descriptions: Rarer than the Bornean orangutan
Spends nearly its entire life in trees
Has been observed making simple tools from sticks
Fewer than 14,000 remain in the wild
Has longer facial hair than Bornean orangutans

gibbon-lar.name: Lar gibbon
descriptions: Can swing through trees at up to 55 km/h
Arms are longer than its legs for brachiation
Mates for life and sings duets with its partner
Morning calls can be heard over 1 km away
Smallest of the apes, weighing up to 8 kg

babouin-olive.name: Olive baboon
descriptions: Lives in troops of up to 150 individuals
Has a complex social hierarchy with alliances
Omnivore that eats almost anything available
Males have large canine teeth for defense
One of the most widespread baboon species in Africa

mandrill.name: Mandrill
descriptions: Most colorful mammal with its blue and red face
Males can weigh up to 35 kg
Lives in the rainforests of central West Africa
Troops called hordes can number over 600
Face colors brighten with excitement or dominance

macaque-japonais.name: Japanese macaque
descriptions: Famous for bathing in hot springs in winter
Northernmost living nonhuman primate
Lives in troops with strict dominance hierarchies
Known to wash food before eating it
Can survive winter temperatures below minus 15 C

nasique.name: Proboscis monkey
descriptions: Males have an enormous drooping nose up to 10 cm
Large nose amplifies warning calls to the group
Excellent swimmer with partially webbed feet
Found only on the island of Borneo
Has a pot belly from digesting tough leaves

lemurien-catta.name: Ring-tailed lemur
descriptions: Tail has 13 alternating black and white rings
Sunbathes in a yoga-like seated position each morning
Males have stink fights using scent glands on wrists
Lives only in southern Madagascar
Groups are led by a dominant female

aye-aye.name: Aye-aye
descriptions: Uses a long thin middle finger to extract grubs
Only primate that uses echolocation-like tapping
Considered a bad omen in Malagasy folklore
Largest nocturnal primate in the world
Continuously growing incisors like a rodent

tarsier-des-philippines.name: Philippine tarsier
descriptions: Each eye is as large as its entire brain
Can rotate its head nearly 180 degrees
Entirely nocturnal insect hunter
One of the smallest primates at about 15 cm tall
Communicates at ultrasonic frequencies

tamarin-lion-dore.name: Golden lion tamarin
descriptions: Golden mane makes it look like a tiny lion
Found only in Brazil's Atlantic coastal rainforest
Weighs only about 600 grams
Saved from extinction by captive breeding programs
Lives in family groups and both parents carry babies

singe-hurleur-roux.name: Red howler monkey
descriptions: Loudest land animal; howls heard over 5 km away
Enlarged hyoid bone acts as a resonating chamber
Spends most of its day resting to conserve energy
Lives in the forests of South America
Tail is prehensile and used as a fifth limb

capucin-brun.name: Tufted capuchin
descriptions: One of the most intelligent New World monkeys
Uses stones to crack open nuts
Named for its cap of fur resembling a monk's hood
Has been trained to assist people with disabilities
Lives in groups of 10 to 35 individuals

elephant-d-afrique.name: African elephant
descriptions: Largest living land animal, up to 6 tonnes
Has over 40,000 muscles in its trunk alone
Can communicate using infrasound over 10 km
Mourns its dead and revisits remains of family
Ears shaped like the continent of Africa

elephant-d-asie.name: Asian elephant
descriptions: Smaller ears than African elephants
Only some males grow tusks in this species
Has been domesticated for thousands of years
One of the few animals that can recognize mirrors
Can eat up to 150 kg of vegetation per day

zebre-des-plaines.name: Plains zebra
descriptions: Each zebra has a unique pattern of stripes
Stripes may confuse biting flies and predators
Lives in herds of up to several hundred
Can run at speeds up to 65 km/h
Most common zebra species in Africa

zebre-de-grevy.name: Grevy's zebra
descriptions: Largest wild equid in the world
Has the narrowest stripes of any zebra
Named after French president Jules Grevy
Endangered with fewer than 2,500 in the wild
Found only in Kenya and Ethiopia

ane-sauvage-d-afrique.name: African wild ass
descriptions: Ancestor of the domestic donkey
Critically endangered with under 600 in the wild
Can survive on very little water in arid habitats
Lives in the deserts of northeast Africa
Can run at speeds up to 50 km/h

cheval-de-przewalski.name: Przewalski's horse
descriptions: Last truly wild horse species
Was extinct in the wild; reintroduced from captivity
Has 66 chromosomes versus 64 in domestic horses
Named after Russian explorer Nikolai Przewalski
Stocky build with a stiff upright mane

rhinoceros-blanc.name: White rhinoceros
descriptions: Second largest land animal after the elephant
Name comes from Dutch 'wijd' meaning wide, not white
Can weigh over 2,000 kg
Has two horns made of compacted keratin
Square-lipped for grazing on grass

rhinoceros-noir.name: Black rhinoceros
descriptions: Hooked upper lip for browsing on leaves and twigs
Critically endangered due to poaching for horns
Can charge at speeds up to 55 km/h
Has poor eyesight but excellent hearing and smell
Smaller than the white rhino at about 1,400 kg

rhinoceros-indien.name: Indian rhinoceros
descriptions: Armor-like skin folds give it a prehistoric look
Has only one horn, unlike African rhinos
Excellent swimmer that can cross rivers easily
Can run at speeds up to 55 km/h
Found in the grasslands of India and Nepal

rhinoceros-de-sumatra.name: Sumatran rhinoceros
descriptions: Smallest living rhinoceros species
Only Asian rhino with two horns
Covered in reddish-brown hair
Fewer than 80 individuals remain in the wild
Closest living relative of the woolly rhinoceros

hippopotame.name: Hippopotamus
descriptions: Third largest land animal after elephant and rhino
Secretes a natural red sunscreen from its skin
Can hold its breath underwater for up to 5 minutes
Responsible for more human deaths than lions in Africa
Can run at up to 30 km/h on land

hippopotame-nain.name: Pygmy hippopotamus
descriptions: About one-tenth the weight of a common hippo
Nocturnal and very secretive in the wild
Found only in West African forests and swamps
Endangered with fewer than 3,000 in the wild
Spends less time in water than the common hippo

girafe.name: Giraffe
descriptions: Tallest living animal at up to 5.8 meters
Heart weighs about 11 kg to pump blood to its head
Sleeps only about 30 minutes per day
Each giraffe has a unique pattern of spots
Tongue is up to 45 cm long and dark purple

okapi.name: Okapi
descriptions: Closest living relative of the giraffe
Striped legs help it blend into forest shadows
Was unknown to Western science until 1901
Found only in the Democratic Republic of Congo
Tongue is long enough to clean its own ears

bison-d-amerique.name: American bison
descriptions: Largest land animal in North America
Can run at speeds up to 55 km/h
Nearly hunted to extinction in the 1800s
Recovered from under 1,000 to over 500,000 today
Calves are orange-red and called red dogs

bison-d-europe.name: European bison
descriptions: Largest wild land animal in Europe
Went extinct in the wild in 1927 and was reintroduced
Can jump 2 meters high and 3 meters wide
Prefers forests unlike the American bison
Over 7,000 now roam in rewilded areas of Europe

buffle-d-afrique.name: African buffalo
descriptions: One of the Big Five game animals of Africa
Herd decisions are made by majority vote
Fused horn base is called a boss, hard as armor
Known to seek revenge on lions and hunters
Herds can number over 1,000 individuals

yack.name: Yak
descriptions: Thrives at altitudes above 4,000 meters
Dense woolly undercoat withstands extreme cold
Wild yaks can weigh up to 1,000 kg
Domesticated for thousands of years in Central Asia
Produces milk richer than cow's milk

gnou-bleu.name: Blue wildebeest
descriptions: Migrates over 1,600 km yearly in the Serengeti
Calves can stand and run within minutes of birth
Over 1.5 million take part in the Great Migration
Also called the wildebeest
Can run at speeds up to 80 km/h

impala.name: Impala
descriptions: Can leap up to 3 meters high and 10 meters far
Lives in herds of up to 100 in African savannas
Males fight for dominance using their lyre-shaped horns
Can change direction mid-leap to escape predators
One of the most common antelopes in Africa

gazelle-de-thomson.name: Thomson's gazelle
descriptions: Second fastest land animal after the cheetah
Named after explorer Joseph Thomson
Distinctive black side stripe on a tan body
Constantly flicks its tail from side to side
Lives in the grasslands of East Africa

oryx-d-arabie.name: Arabian oryx
descriptions: Was extinct in the wild and successfully reintroduced
Can detect rain from over 100 km away
Horns can grow up to 70 cm straight and long
Has reflective white coat to deflect desert heat
National animal of Oman and Qatar

addax.name: Addax
descriptions: One of the rarest mammals on Earth
Adapted to survive in the Sahara Desert
Can go almost a year without drinking water
Hooves are wide and flat for walking on sand
Critically endangered with under 100 in the wild

bouquetin-des-alpes.name: Alpine ibex
descriptions: Males have curved horns up to one meter long
Climbs near-vertical cliffs with ease
Was nearly hunted to extinction by the 1800s
Lives at altitudes above 2,500 meters in summer
Fights for mates by clashing horns head-on

chamois.name: Chamois
descriptions: Can leap 2 meters high and 6 meters far
Hooves have rubber-like soles for grip on rocks
Lives in the mountains of Europe and western Asia
Horn hooks are used to classify age and sex
Whistles sharply to warn the herd of danger

mouflon-de-corse.name: Corsican mouflon
descriptions: Ancestor of all modern domestic sheep breeds
Males have large spiraling horns
Found naturally only on Corsica and Sardinia
Lives in mountainous terrain and steep hillsides
Endangered in its native island range

saiga.name: Saiga antelope
descriptions: Has a bizarre bulbous nose that filters dust
Nose also warms cold air before it reaches lungs
Lives on the steppes of Central Asia
Can run at speeds up to 80 km/h
Critically endangered due to poaching and disease

koudou-grand.name: Greater kudu
descriptions: Males have spiral horns up to 1.8 meters
Can jump fences over 2.5 meters high
Lives in woodland and bushland of eastern Africa
Has 6 to 10 vertical white stripes on its body
One of the tallest antelopes at 1.5 meters shoulder

cerf-elaphe.name: Red deer
descriptions: Males grow and shed antlers every year
Antlers can weigh up to 15 kg combined
Roars during rutting season to attract mates
One of the largest deer species in Europe
Velvet on antlers supplies blood during growth

chevreuil.name: Roe deer
descriptions: Most common deer species in Europe
Males have short antlers with usually three points
Fawns have white spots for camouflage
Barks like a dog when alarmed
Can delay embryo implantation by several months

elan.name: Moose
descriptions: Largest deer species in the world
Antlers can span up to 1.8 meters across
Excellent swimmer that can dive for aquatic plants
Has a flap of skin called a bell under its chin
Can run at up to 56 km/h despite its size

renne.name: Reindeer
descriptions: Only deer species where females also have antlers
Migrates the longest distance of any land mammal
Nose warms air before it reaches the lungs
Hooves change texture from soft in summer to hard in winter
Also known as caribou in North America

daim-europeen.name: Fallow deer
descriptions: Males have distinctive flat palmate antlers
Was introduced across Europe by the Romans
Often kept in deer parks since medieval times
Can run at speeds up to 48 km/h
Has a spotted coat that fades in winter

muntjac-de-reeves.name: Reeves's muntjac
descriptions: One of the smallest deer species in the world
Males have short antlers and long canine tusks
Barks like a dog when disturbed, earning its nickname
Native to China but introduced to England
Also called the barking deer

cerf-sika.name: Sika deer
descriptions: Sacred in Japan and roams freely in Nara
Keeps its spotted coat year-round in some subspecies
Males whistle rather than roar during the rut
Native to East Asia but introduced worldwide
Can hybridize with red deer where ranges overlap

dromadaire.name: Dromedary camel
descriptions: Has one hump that stores up to 36 kg of fat
Can drink 200 liters of water in 3 minutes
Body temperature can fluctuate to reduce sweating
Has three eyelids to protect from sandstorms
No wild populations exist; all are domesticated

chameau-de-bactriane.name: Bactrian camel
descriptions: Has two humps unlike the dromedary's one
Wild Bactrian camel is critically endangered
Survives temperatures from minus 40 to plus 50 C
Can close its nostrils to keep out blowing sand
Native to the steppes of Central Asia

lama.name: Llama
descriptions: Domesticated from wild guanacos 6,000 years ago
Used as pack animals in the Andes for centuries
Spits when agitated or to establish dominance
Hums to communicate with each other
Social animal that needs companionship to thrive

alpaga.name: Alpaca
descriptions: Fiber is softer and warmer than sheep's wool
Domesticated by the Incas over 5,000 years ago
Smaller and more timid than llamas
Comes in over 22 natural fiber colors
Lives at high altitudes in the Andes

vigogne.name: Vicuña
descriptions: Produces the world's finest natural fiber
Wild ancestor of the alpaca
Was sacred to the Incas and reserved for royalty
Lives at altitudes above 3,500 meters in the Andes
Was near extinction but recovered through protection

sanglier.name: Wild boar
descriptions: Ancestor of the domestic pig
Has a sharp sense of smell for finding food
Males have sharp tusks used for defense
Can run at speeds up to 40 km/h
Found across Europe, Asia, and North Africa

phacochere.name: Common warthog
descriptions: Runs with its tail held straight up like an antenna
Kneels on its front legs to feed on grass
Has two pairs of large tusks on its face
Sleeps in abandoned aardvark burrows
Can run at speeds up to 48 km/h from predators

babiroussa.name: Babirusa
descriptions: Upper tusks grow through the top of its snout
Found only on the Indonesian island of Sulawesi
Name means pig-deer in Malay
Males' tusks can curve back toward their skull
One of the most unusual-looking wild pigs

tapir-de-malaisie.name: Malayan tapir
descriptions: Striking black and white coloring breaks up its shape
Largest tapir species, weighing up to 350 kg
Excellent swimmer that uses rivers to escape predators
Has a short prehensile trunk-like snout
Found in the forests of Southeast Asia

tapir-terrestre.name: South American tapir
descriptions: Largest native land mammal in South America
Uses its flexible snout to grab leaves and fruit
Babies are born with stripes and spots for camouflage
Excellent swimmer and diver
Considered a living fossil with little evolution in millions of years

kangourou-roux.name: Red kangaroo
descriptions: Largest marsupial and largest living kangaroo species
Can leap over 9 meters in a single bound
Males box each other for mating rights
Joey stays in the pouch for about 8 months
Can travel at 56 km/h over short distances

wallaby-de-bennett.name: Bennett's wallaby
descriptions: Also known as the red-necked wallaby
Smaller than kangaroos but hops the same way
Found in forests of eastern Australia and Tasmania
Mostly solitary except when feeding in groups
Can survive in surprisingly cold climates

koala.name: Koala
descriptions: Sleeps up to 22 hours per day
Eats exclusively eucalyptus leaves which are toxic
Has fingerprints almost identical to human ones
Baby koalas eat their mother's pap for gut bacteria
Not a bear despite being called a koala bear

wombat-commun.name: Common wombat
descriptions: Produces cube-shaped droppings
Has a backward-facing pouch to avoid filling with dirt
Can run at speeds up to 40 km/h
Burrows can be over 200 meters long
Uses its reinforced rump to block predators from burrows

quokka.name: Quokka
descriptions: Known as the world's happiest animal for its smile
Found almost exclusively on Rottnest Island, Australia
Can survive long periods without water
About the size of a domestic cat
Dutch explorers mistook them for giant rats

opossum-de-virginie.name: Virginia opossum
descriptions: Only marsupial native to North America
Plays dead when threatened, called playing possum
Has more teeth than any other North American mammal
Prehensile tail can grip branches like a fifth hand
Immune to most snake venom and rabies

diable-de-tasmanie.name: Tasmanian devil
descriptions: Strongest bite relative to body size of any mammal
Found only on the island of Tasmania
Screams and screeches loudly when feeding
Can eat up to 40 percent of its body weight in a day
Threatened by a contagious facial tumor disease

numbat.name: Numbat
descriptions: One of the only fully diurnal marsupials
Eats up to 20,000 termites per day
Has a long sticky tongue about 10 cm long
Found only in small pockets of Western Australia
Has distinctive reddish-brown fur with white stripes

ornithorynque.name: Platypus
descriptions: One of only five mammals that lay eggs
Males have venomous spurs on their hind legs
Detects prey with electroreceptors in its bill
Has a beaver-like tail and duck-like bill
Scientists thought the first specimen was a hoax

echidne-a-nez-court.name: Short-beaked echidna
descriptions: One of only five egg-laying mammals on Earth
Covered in sharp spines and coarse hair
Has no teeth and crushes food between tongue and palate
Can live over 50 years in captivity
Curls into a spiny ball when threatened

renard-volant.name: Flying fox
descriptions: Largest bat species with a wingspan of up to 1.7 m
Not a fox; it is a fruit-eating megabat
Navigates using excellent eyesight, not echolocation
Pollinates flowers and spreads seeds
Roosts in huge colonies called camps

chauve-souris-fer-a-cheval.name: Greater horseshoe bat
descriptions: Named for the horseshoe-shaped nose leaf on its face
Emits echolocation calls through its nose, not mouth
Found across Europe, Asia, and North Africa
Hibernates in caves during winter months
Hunts moths and other insects in flight

pipistrelle-commune.name: Common pipistrelle
descriptions: One of the most common bats in Europe
Weighs only about 5 grams, less than a coin
Can eat 3,000 insects in a single night
Uses echolocation at frequencies around 45 kHz
Fits easily in the palm of a hand

vampire-commun.name: Common vampire bat
descriptions: Only bat that feeds entirely on blood
Can run on the ground using its wings as front legs
Shares blood meals with hungry roost mates
Saliva contains an anticoagulant called draculin
Heat sensors on its nose locate blood vessels

herisson-d-europe.name: European hedgehog
descriptions: Has about 5,000 spines on its back
Curls into a tight ball when threatened
Can swim and climb surprisingly well
Hibernates through winter in a nest of leaves
Eats slugs, insects, and even small snakes

taupe-d-europe.name: European mole
descriptions: Can dig 20 meters of tunnel in a single day
Has velvety fur that moves in any direction
Front paws are like shovels with extra thumb bones
Nearly blind but has excellent hearing and touch
Eats about half its body weight in worms daily

musaraigne-pygmee.name: Eurasian pygmy shrew
descriptions: Smallest mammal in Europe by weight at 3 grams
Heart beats up to 1,200 times per minute
Must eat every 2 hours or risk starvation
Has a venomous bite to subdue prey
So small it can fit through a ballpoint pen hole

tenrec-raye.name: Lowland streaked tenrec
descriptions: Can vibrate its quills to communicate with others
Found only on the island of Madagascar
Looks like a cross between a hedgehog and a shrew
Only mammal known to use stridulation like insects
Has the most teeth of any land mammal: up to 40

castor-d-europe.name: Eurasian beaver
descriptions: Builds dams that can be over 100 meters long
Second largest rodent in the world
Teeth are orange because they contain iron
Creates entire wetland ecosystems with its dams
Was nearly extinct in Europe but is now recovering

ecureuil-roux.name: Red squirrel
descriptions: Buries thousands of nuts but forgets many of them
Forgotten nuts grow into new trees, aiding forests
Tail is used for balance, warmth, and signaling
Can jump over 2 meters between branches
Ear tufts grow longer in winter

marmotte-des-alpes.name: Alpine marmot
descriptions: Hibernates for up to 6 months each year
Heart rate drops from 200 to 30 beats per minute
Whistles loudly to warn of predators like eagles
Lives in colonies at altitudes above 1,000 meters
Can lose a third of its body weight during winter

chien-de-prairie.name: Prairie dog
descriptions: Has one of the most complex languages in animals
Can describe a predator's color, size, and speed
Lives in huge underground towns called coteries
Greets others with a kiss-like touch of teeth
Named for its bark-like warning call

capybara.name: Capybara
descriptions: Largest living rodent, weighing up to 65 kg
Semi-aquatic and an excellent swimmer
Can hold its breath underwater for up to 5 minutes
Extremely social and gets along with many species
Has webbed feet for swimming

chinchilla.name: Chinchilla
descriptions: Has the densest fur of any land animal
Up to 20,000 hairs per square centimeter
Bathes in volcanic dust to keep fur clean
Can jump up to 1.8 meters high
Critically endangered in the wild in the Andes

porc-epic-a-crete.name: Crested porcupine
descriptions: Quills can be over 30 cm long
Rattles its tail quills as a warning to predators
Cannot shoot its quills but they detach on contact
Largest rodent in Europe, Africa, and Asia
Gnaws on bones for calcium and to sharpen teeth

rat-musque.name: Muskrat
descriptions: Named for musky smell from glands near its tail
Semi-aquatic with partially webbed hind feet
Builds lodges in marshes similar to beaver dams
Native to North America but invasive in Europe
Can swim underwater for up to 15 minutes

hamster-commun.name: European hamster
descriptions: Has expandable cheek pouches to carry food
Can carry half its body weight in its cheeks
Much larger than pet hamsters at about 30 cm
Hibernates in deep burrows during winter
Critically endangered in its native European range

lemming-de-norvege.name: Norway lemming
descriptions: Population booms and crashes in 3 to 4 year cycles
Does not actually jump off cliffs, that is a myth
Brightly colored fur warns predators of its aggression
Lives in the tundra of Scandinavia
Will fight back aggressively when cornered

gerbille-de-mongolie.name: Mongolian gerbil
descriptions: One of the most popular small pets worldwide
Thumps its hind legs to warn of danger
Native to the steppes of Mongolia and China
Highly social and lives in family groups
Can jump up to 30 cm high from a standstill

lapin-de-garenne.name: European rabbit
descriptions: Ancestor of all domestic rabbit breeds
Lives in complex underground warrens
Can run at up to 56 km/h in short bursts
Eats its own droppings to extract more nutrients
Hind legs are powerful enough to thump warnings

lievre-d-europe.name: European hare
descriptions: Can run at speeds up to 70 km/h
Born fully furred with open eyes, unlike rabbits
Does not burrow but rests in shallow depressions
Famous for 'boxing matches' during mating season
Ears are longer than its head for heat regulation

pika-americain.name: American pika
descriptions: Related to rabbits but looks like a hamster
Lives on rocky mountain slopes in North America
Collects and dries hay for winter food stores
Calls with a sharp 'eek' to defend territory
Very sensitive to warming temperatures

tatou-a-neuf-bandes.name: Nine-banded armadillo
descriptions: Always gives birth to identical quadruplets
Has a hard bony shell covering its body
Can hold its breath for up to 6 minutes underwater
Inflates intestines with air to float across rivers
Only armadillo found in the United States

tatou-geant.name: Giant armadillo
descriptions: Largest armadillo species, weighing up to 50 kg
Has more teeth than any other land mammal: up to 100
Front claws can be over 20 cm long
Digs huge burrows used by many other species
Nocturnal and very rarely seen in the wild

paresseux-a-trois-doigts.name: Brown-throated sloth
descriptions: Moves so slowly that algae grows on its fur
Can rotate its head nearly 270 degrees
Descends to the ground only to defecate once a week
Sleeps about 15 hours a day in the tree canopy
Can swim three times faster than it moves on land

paresseux-a-deux-doigts.name: Two-toed sloth
descriptions: Larger and faster than three-toed sloths
Nocturnal while three-toed sloths are diurnal
Has only two fingers on its front limbs
Hangs upside down for most of its life
Internal organs are attached to ribs for hanging

fourmilier-geant.name: Giant anteater
descriptions: Tongue is about 60 cm long and sticky
Can flick its tongue 150 times per minute
Has no teeth at all
Eats up to 35,000 ants and termites per day
Claws are so powerful it can rip open concrete nests

tamandua-du-sud.name: Southern tamandua
descriptions: Smaller relative of the giant anteater
Has a prehensile tail for climbing trees
Releases a foul smell when threatened, like a skunk
Eats ants, termites, and bees
Found in forests and savannas of South America

pangolin-de-chine.name: Chinese pangolin
descriptions: Most trafficked mammal in the world
Covered in tough overlapping keratin scales
Rolls into an armored ball when threatened
Has no teeth; uses a sticky tongue to eat ants
Critically endangered due to illegal wildlife trade

pangolin-geant.name: Giant pangolin
descriptions: Largest pangolin species, up to 1.8 meters long
Can weigh up to 33 kg with its heavy scales
Walks on its hind legs with front claws curled
Tears open termite mounds with powerful claws
Found in the forests of Central and West Africa

lamantin-des-caraibes.name: West Indian manatee
descriptions: Also called the sea cow for its gentle grazing
Eats up to 10 percent of its body weight daily
Can weigh over 1,500 kg
Has no natural predators in its habitat
Sailors once mistook manatees for mermaids

dugong.name: Dugong
descriptions: Only strictly marine herbivorous mammal
Grazes on sea grass meadows on the ocean floor
Can live over 70 years in the wild
Closest living relative of the elephant family
Found in warm coastal waters of the Indo-Pacific

oryctorope.name: Aardvark
descriptions: Name means 'earth pig' in Afrikaans
Can dig a burrow in soft soil in 5 minutes
Has a long sticky tongue for eating termites
Entirely nocturnal and very hard to spot in the wild
Teeth grow continuously and have no enamel

daman-des-rochers.name: Rock hyrax
descriptions: Surprisingly, its closest relative is the elephant
Lives in rocky outcrops across Africa and the Middle East
Has padded feet that act like suction cups on rocks
Makes complex songs lasting several minutes
About the size of a rabbit but not a rodent

suricata.name: Common palm civet
descriptions: Sentinels stand guard and bark warnings to the group
Adults teach young to eat scorpions by removing stings
Lives in groups called mobs of up to 30
Immune to some scorpion and snake venoms
Found in the Kalahari and Namib deserts

binturong.name: Binturong
descriptions: Smells like buttered popcorn due to a chemical compound
Also called the bearcat though it is neither
Has a prehensile tail that grips branches like a hand
One of only two carnivores with a prehensile tail
Lives in the dense forests of Southeast Asia

genette-commune.name: Common genet
descriptions: Looks like a cross between a cat and a weasel
Has retractable claws like a cat
Excellent night hunter with superb night vision
Was kept as a pet in medieval Europe for pest control
Can squeeze through any gap its head fits through

kinkajou.name: Kinkajou
descriptions: Has a prehensile tail and is fully arboreal
Also called the honey bear for its love of nectar
Can turn its feet backward to run along branches
Pollinates trees as it drinks flower nectar
Related to raccoons, not primates or bears

zibeline.name: Sable
descriptions: Prized for having one of the finest furs in the world
Lives in dense forests of Russia and northern Asia
Excellent climber and hunter of small mammals
Can jump between trees with great agility
Omnivore that also eats berries and pine nuts

putois-d-europe.name: European polecat
descriptions: Ancestor of the domestic ferret
Sprays a foul-smelling musk when threatened
Hunts rabbits in their burrows
Has a distinctive bandit-like face mask
Name comes from French for 'stinking chicken'

hyene-rayee.name: Striped hyena
descriptions: Largest of the hyena species by length
Has a distinctive crest of long hair along its back
Mostly a scavenger unlike the spotted hyena
Found from North Africa to Central Asia
Can crack open large bones with its strong jaws

protele.name: Aardwolf
descriptions: A hyena that eats almost exclusively termites
Can eat 300,000 termites in a single night
Has small, peg-like teeth unlike other hyenas
Also known as the aardwolf, meaning 'earth wolf'
Lives in the grasslands of eastern and southern Africa

aigle-royal.name: Golden eagle
descriptions: Can spot a rabbit from over 3 km away
Dives at speeds up to 320 km/h
Wingspan reaches up to 2.3 meters
Mates for life and reuses the same nest for years
Symbol of power used on many national emblems

pygargue-a-tete-blanche.name: Bald eagle
descriptions: National bird and symbol of the United States
Does not get its white head until age 5
Builds the largest nests of any bird, up to 2 tonnes
Was nearly extinct from DDT but recovered fully
Snatches fish from the water with its talons

aigle-des-singes.name: Philippine eagle
descriptions: National bird of the Philippines
One of the largest and rarest eagles in the world
Wingspan reaches up to 2 meters
Hunts monkeys, flying lemurs, and large snakes
Critically endangered with about 800 left

harpie-feroce.name: Harpy eagle
descriptions: Most powerful eagle in the world
Talons are as large as a grizzly bear's claws
Can carry prey weighing up to half its body weight
Hunts sloths and monkeys in the rainforest canopy
Found in Central and South American tropical forests

buse-variable.name: Common buzzard
descriptions: Most common bird of prey in Europe
Plumage varies greatly from dark brown to almost white
Soars in wide circles on thermal currents
Hunts small mammals, especially voles and rabbits
Mewing call is a classic sound of the countryside

milan-royal.name: Red kite
descriptions: Forked tail makes it unmistakable in flight
Was once common as a scavenger in medieval London
Can adjust its tail like a rudder while soaring
Feeds on carrion, worms, and small animals
Successfully reintroduced to the UK in the 1990s

vautour-fauve.name: Griffon vulture
descriptions: Can soar for hours without flapping its wings
Bald head stays clean while feeding inside carcasses
Stomach acid kills anthrax, cholera, and botulism
Wingspan can exceed 2.8 meters
Essential to ecosystems as a natural sanitation crew

gypaete-barbu.name: Bearded vulture
descriptions: Drops bones from height onto rocks to crack them open
Only bird that feeds almost exclusively on bones
Also called the bearded vulture for its bristly beard
Rubs iron-rich mud on its feathers for color
Wingspan reaches up to 2.8 meters

condor-des-andes.name: Andean condor
descriptions: Largest flying bird in the world by wing area
Wingspan can exceed 3.2 meters
Can soar to altitudes above 5,000 meters
Lives in the Andes mountains of South America
Sacred to many Andean cultures for centuries

condor-de-californie.name: California condor
descriptions: Was down to only 22 birds in 1987
Largest flying bird in North America
Can glide for miles without flapping its wings
Has a wingspan of up to 2.9 meters
Slowly recovering through intensive breeding programs

faucon-pelerin.name: Peregrine falcon
descriptions: Fastest animal on Earth, diving at over 380 km/h
Found on every continent except Antarctica
Has a special notch in its beak to kill prey quickly
Recovered from near extinction after DDT was banned
Now nests on skyscrapers in major cities

faucon-crecerelle.name: Common kestrel
descriptions: Can hover in place by flying into the wind
Can see ultraviolet light to track rodent urine trails
Most common falcon in Europe
Nests in old buildings, cliffs, and tree holes
Hunts mostly voles and mice in open fields

secretaire.name: Secretarybird
descriptions: Stomps snakes to death with its powerful legs
Named for quill-like head feathers resembling a clerk
Can walk over 30 km per day hunting for prey
Stands up to 1.3 meters tall on long legs
Only raptor that hunts primarily on foot

epervier-d-europe.name: Eurasian sparrowhawk
descriptions: Specializes in hunting small birds in dense cover
Female is up to 25 percent larger than the male
Short rounded wings allow agile flight through trees
Can accelerate rapidly to surprise prey in gardens
One of the most widespread raptors in Europe

balbuzard-pecheur.name: Osprey
descriptions: Feet have reversible outer toes for gripping fish
Dives feet-first into water to catch fish
Found on every continent except Antarctica
Soles have spiny pads for holding slippery fish
Builds enormous stick nests near water

grand-duc-d-europe.name: Eurasian eagle-owl
descriptions: Largest owl species in the world
Wingspan can reach 1.9 meters
Can take prey as large as foxes and young deer
Deep hooting call carries over several kilometers
Eyes are fixed in their sockets; it must turn its head

chouette-hulotte.name: Tawny owl
descriptions: Most common owl in Europe
Famous 'twit-twoo' call is actually a duet of two owls
Excellent night vision, 100 times better than human
Silent flight due to serrated feather edges
Highly territorial and aggressive near its nest

chouette-harfang.name: Snowy owl
descriptions: One of the few owls active during the day
Males are almost entirely white; females are spotted
Lives in the Arctic tundra of North America and Eurasia
Can eat up to 5 lemmings per day
Made famous as Hedwig in the Harry Potter series

chevechette-d-europe.name: Eurasian pygmy owl
descriptions: One of the smallest owls in Europe at 16 cm
Hunts during the day unlike most owls
Stores surplus prey in tree holes like a pantry
Has false eye spots on the back of its head
Bobs its head up and down when curious

effraie-des-clochers.name: Barn owl
descriptions: Heart-shaped face acts as a satellite dish for sound
Can hunt in complete darkness using hearing alone
Found on every continent except Antarctica
Silent flight earned it the nickname ghost owl
Often nests in church steeples and old barns

hibou-moyen-duc.name: Long-eared owl
descriptions: Ear tufts are not ears but display feathers
Real ears are asymmetrical for pinpointing sound
Roosts in dense vegetation during the day
Can make itself appear very thin to hide on branches
Hunts small mammals in open fields at night

ara-bleu.name: Blue-and-yellow macaw
descriptions: Blue and gold feathers are unmistakable
Can live over 60 years in captivity
Mates for life and pairs are rarely apart
Strong beak can crack Brazil nuts easily
Lives in the rainforests of South America

ara-rouge.name: Scarlet macaw
descriptions: Bright red, yellow, and blue plumage
National bird of Honduras
Can fly at speeds up to 56 km/h
Eats clay from riverbanks to neutralize plant toxins
Can live more than 50 years in the wild

ara-hyacinthe.name: Hyacinth macaw
descriptions: Largest macaw and largest flying parrot species
Striking cobalt-blue plumage with yellow eye rings
Beak can crack macadamia and coconut shells
About 6,500 remain in the wild in South America
Can grow up to one meter from head to tail

perroquet-gris-du-gabon.name: African grey parrot
descriptions: Considered the most intelligent parrot species
Can learn hundreds of words and use them in context
Alex, a famous grey parrot, could count and name colors
Lives in the forests of West and Central Africa
Endangered due to the pet trade and habitat loss

cacatoes-a-huppe-jaune.name: Sulphur-crested cockatoo
descriptions: Raises its bright yellow crest when excited
Can live over 80 years in captivity
Extremely social and forms large flocks
Known for its loud screeching calls
Native to Australia and New Guinea

kakapo.name: Kakapo
descriptions: Only flightless parrot in the world
One of the longest-lived birds, up to 90 years
Nocturnal and has a strong sweet body odor
Males inflate like a balloon and boom to attract mates
Critically endangered with about 250 individuals left

kea.name: Kea
descriptions: World's only alpine parrot
Extremely curious and known to disassemble car parts
Lives in the mountains of New Zealand's South Island
Highly intelligent with complex social behaviors
Can solve multi-step puzzles for food rewards

perruche-ondulee.name: Budgerigar
descriptions: One of the most popular pet birds worldwide
Can learn to say 100 or more words
Native to the dry interior of Australia
Wild birds are always green and yellow
Flocks can number in the tens of thousands

inseparable-de-fischer.name: Fischer's lovebird
descriptions: Named after German explorer Gustav Fischer
Mates form strong lifelong pair bonds
Tucks nesting material in its rump feathers
Native to a small area of Tanzania
Popular pet for its colorful green and orange plumage

manchot-empereur.name: Emperor penguin
descriptions: Tallest penguin species at up to 1.2 meters
Breeds during the Antarctic winter at minus 60 C
Males incubate eggs on their feet for 2 months
Can dive over 500 meters deep for fish
Huddles in groups to conserve warmth in blizzards

manchot-royal.name: King penguin
descriptions: Second largest penguin species after the emperor
Has a bright orange patch on each side of its head
Chick-rearing takes over a year, the longest of any bird
Can dive over 300 meters to catch fish and squid
Breeds on sub-Antarctic islands in huge colonies

manchot-adelie.name: Adelie penguin
descriptions: Most widely distributed penguin in Antarctica
Builds nests from small stones on the ground
Males offer pebbles to females as courtship gifts
Can swim at speeds up to 45 km/h
Named after the wife of French explorer Dumont d'Urville

manchot-du-cap.name: African penguin
descriptions: Also called the African penguin or jackass penguin
Brays like a donkey, earning its nickname
Lives along the coast of South Africa and Namibia
Endangered with population declining rapidly
Pink glands above its eyes help regulate temperature

gorfou-sauteur.name: Southern rockhopper penguin
descriptions: Hops with both feet together on rocky shores
Has spiky yellow eyebrow crests and red eyes
Aggressive and noisy among penguin species
Can jump up to 1.5 meters between rocks
Breeds on remote sub-Antarctic islands

flamant-rose.name: Greater flamingo
descriptions: Pink color comes from pigments in shrimp and algae
Feeds with its head upside down in water
Can stand on one leg for hours to conserve heat
Lives in huge flocks of up to hundreds of thousands
Chicks are born white and turn pink over time

flamant-des-caraibes.name: American flamingo
descriptions: Brightest and most colorful flamingo species
Deep crimson plumage due to high carotenoid diet
Found in the Caribbean, Galapagos, and northern South America
Builds mud mound nests in shallow lagoons
National bird of the Bahamas

flamant-du-chili.name: Chilean flamingo
descriptions: Distinguished by grey legs with pink knee joints
Found in South American salt lakes and estuaries
Feeds on algae, diatoms, and small crustaceans
Can filter up to 20 liters of water per day
Often lives at high-altitude Andean lakes

colibri-a-gorge-rubis.name: Ruby-throated hummingbird
descriptions: Heart beats over 1,200 times per minute in flight
Can fly backward, the only bird group that can
Wings beat up to 80 times per second
Migrates nonstop across the Gulf of Mexico
Weighs less than a nickel at about 3 grams

colibri-d-anna.name: Anna's hummingbird
descriptions: Male's head feathers flash hot pink in sunlight
One of the few hummingbirds that sing a real song
Can enter torpor at night to save energy
Found along the Pacific coast of North America
Males perform dramatic J-shaped dive displays

colibri-porte-epee.name: Sword-billed hummingbird
descriptions: Has the longest bill relative to body of any bird
Bill is longer than its entire body excluding tail
Co-evolved with long tubular flowers in the Andes
Found in cloud forests of Venezuela to Bolivia
Hovers to feed on nectar deep inside flowers

merle-noir.name: Common blackbird
descriptions: One of the most melodious songbirds in Europe
Males are jet black with a bright orange bill
Sings from rooftops at dawn and dusk
Eats earthworms, berries, and insects
Adapts easily to gardens, parks, and urban areas

rouge-gorge-familier.name: European robin
descriptions: Red breast helps defend territory against rivals
Sings year-round, even in winter and at night
Follows gardeners to snatch unearthed worms
Very territorial despite its friendly appearance
National bird of the United Kingdom

mesange-bleue.name: Eurasian blue tit
descriptions: Blue cap and yellow underparts are distinctive
Hangs upside down to reach insects on branches
Can eat hundreds of caterpillars per day
Commonly visits garden bird feeders across Europe
UV coloring invisible to humans helps attract mates

mesange-charbonniere.name: Great tit
descriptions: Largest tit species in Europe
Has been observed using tools to extract food
Bold and dominant at bird feeders
Black stripe down its belly varies by sex
Learned to open milk bottle caps in Britain

moineau-domestique.name: House sparrow
descriptions: One of the most widespread birds on Earth
Lives alongside humans on every continent
Males have a black bib that signals dominance
Population is declining in many European cities
Originally native to Europe and parts of Asia

hirondelle-rustique.name: Barn swallow
descriptions: Migrates up to 11,000 km between breeding grounds
Deeply forked tail aids agile flight catching insects
Builds mud nests on buildings and under bridges
Can drink while flying by skimming water surfaces
One of the most widespread landbirds in the world

corbeau-freux.name: Rook
descriptions: Nests in large noisy colonies called rookeries
Has a pale patch at the base of its bill as an adult
Highly social and often feeds in large flocks
Can use tools and solve complex problems
Found across Europe and western Asia

pie-bavarde.name: Eurasian magpie
descriptions: One of the most intelligent birds in the world
Can recognize itself in a mirror
Attracted to shiny objects, though less than myth says
Long iridescent tail makes up half its body length
Bold and noisy, often found near human settlements

geai-des-chenes.name: Eurasian jay
descriptions: Buries thousands of acorns each autumn for winter
Can mimic the calls of other birds and even cats
Forgotten buried acorns help grow new oak trees
Has a bright blue wing patch and pink plumage
Acts as a forest alarm, shrieking at predators

grand-corbeau.name: Common raven
descriptions: Largest songbird in the world
Can live over 20 years in the wild
Performs aerial acrobatics including barrel rolls
Extremely intelligent; can plan for the future
Found across the Northern Hemisphere

choucas-des-tours.name: Western jackdaw
descriptions: Smallest crow species in Europe
Has distinctive pale grey eyes
Nests in church towers, chimneys, and cliff holes
Highly social and forms lifelong pair bonds
Can learn to open complex latches and locks

etourneau-sansonnet.name: Common starling
descriptions: Forms enormous murmurations of thousands of birds
Excellent mimic of sounds including phone ringtones
Iridescent plumage shimmers green and purple
Introduced to North America by Shakespeare fans
Winter flocks can number over a million birds

rossignol-philomele.name: Common nightingale
descriptions: Famous for singing at night during breeding season
Song has over 200 different phrases
Inspired poets and musicians for centuries
Plain brown plumage makes it hard to spot
Migrates from Europe to Africa for winter

pinson-des-arbres.name: Common chaffinch
descriptions: One of the most common birds in Europe
Males have a colorful blue-grey head and pink breast
Regional song dialects differ across its range
Eats seeds in winter and insects in summer
Can be found in forests, parks, and gardens

chardonneret-elegant.name: European goldfinch
descriptions: Red face, black and white head, gold wing bars
Loves thistle and sunflower seeds
Has a tinkling, liquid song
Popular cage bird for centuries for its beauty
Often seen hanging acrobatically from seed heads

bouvreuil-pivoine.name: Eurasian bullfinch
descriptions: Male has a striking rose-pink breast
Quiet and shy despite its bright coloring
Feeds mainly on buds and seeds of trees
Soft piping call is easy to overlook
Found in woodland and hedgerows across Eurasia

martin-pecheur-d-europe.name: Common kingfisher
descriptions: Brilliant blue and orange plumage
Dives headfirst into water to catch fish
Can judge fish depth by adjusting for light refraction
Nests in riverbank tunnels up to a meter deep
Inspired the design of the Japanese bullet train nose

paradisier-bleu.name: Blue bird-of-paradise
descriptions: Males perform elaborate upside-down courtship displays
Brilliant blue plumage spreads into a skirt-like fan
Found only in the mountains of Papua New Guinea
Females are plain brown for camouflage on the nest
One of over 40 species of birds-of-paradise

oiseau-lyre-superbe.name: Superb lyrebird
descriptions: Males have lyre-shaped tail feathers
Can perfectly mimic chainsaws, cameras, and car alarms
One of the world's greatest vocal mimics
Dances on a cleared mound of soil during courtship
Found in the forests of southeastern Australia

troglodyte-mignon.name: Eurasian wren
descriptions: One of the smallest birds in Europe at 9 cm
Sings an incredibly loud song for its tiny size
Builds multiple dome nests; female chooses the best
Holds its short tail nearly vertical while perching
Found across Europe, Asia, and North America

cardinal-rouge.name: Northern cardinal
descriptions: Bright red male is one of North America's most iconic birds
Female is a warm brown with red tinges
Sings a loud, clear whistle year-round
Named for Catholic cardinals' red robes
State bird of seven US states

cigogne-blanche.name: White stork
descriptions: Migrates from Europe to Africa each year
Builds huge nests on rooftops and chimneys
Nests can weigh over 200 kg after years of use
Symbol of good luck and baby delivery in folklore
Clatters its bill loudly instead of singing

heron-cendre.name: Grey heron
descriptions: Stands motionless for hours waiting to strike at fish
Can swallow fish up to half a meter long
Flies with its neck folded in an S-shape
Largest heron in Europe at about 1 meter tall
Found near freshwater across Europe, Asia, and Africa

grande-aigrette.name: Great egret
descriptions: Was hunted nearly to extinction for its plumes
Bright white plumage and long elegant neck
Grows long breeding plumes during mating season
Found on every continent except Antarctica
Symbol of the National Audubon Society

ibis-rouge.name: Scarlet ibis
descriptions: Brilliant scarlet color comes from carotenoid pigments
Lives in tropical wetlands of South America
Probes mud with its long curved bill for crabs
National bird of Trinidad and Tobago
Chicks are born with grey-brown feathers

spatule-blanche.name: Eurasian spoonbill
descriptions: Sweeps its spoon-shaped bill side to side in water
Bill has sensitive nerve endings to detect prey
Feeds on small fish, insects, and crustaceans
Flies with neck extended, unlike herons
Found in wetlands across Europe and Asia

pelican-blanc.name: Great white pelican
descriptions: Throat pouch holds up to 13 liters of water
Fishes cooperatively in groups herding fish together
Wingspan can reach over 3.6 meters
One of the largest flying birds in the world
Migrates in large V-shaped formations

grand-cormoran.name: Great cormorant
descriptions: Dives underwater to catch fish up to 9 meters deep
Stands with wings spread to dry them after diving
Feathers are less waterproof than other water birds
Used by fishermen in Asia for fishing for centuries
Found worldwide on coasts and inland waters

fou-de-bassan.name: Northern gannet
descriptions: Plunge-dives from 30 meters high at 100 km/h
Has air sacs in its face to cushion the impact
No external nostrils to prevent water entry when diving
Breeds in huge colonies on sea cliffs
Wingspan reaches nearly 2 meters

fregate-superbe.name: Magnificent frigatebird
descriptions: Males inflate a bright red throat pouch to attract mates
Has the largest wingspan-to-body ratio of any bird
Cannot land on water as its feathers are not waterproof
Steals food from other seabirds in mid-flight
Can stay aloft for weeks without landing

autruche.name: Common ostrich
descriptions: Largest and heaviest living bird on Earth
Can run at speeds up to 70 km/h
Lays the largest eggs of any living bird
Eyes are larger than its brain
Cannot fly but kicks powerfully for defense

emeu-d-australie.name: Emu
descriptions: Second largest bird in the world after the ostrich
Males incubate eggs and raise chicks alone
Cannot fly but can run at up to 50 km/h
Has double-shafted feathers that look like fur
Featured on the Australian coat of arms

casoar-a-casque.name: Southern cassowary
descriptions: Often called the world's most dangerous bird
Can kick with lethal dagger-like inner claws
Has a bony casque on top of its head
Third tallest and second heaviest living bird
Crucial for spreading seeds in rainforests

kiwi-austral.name: Southern brown kiwi
descriptions: Has nostrils at the tip of its bill for sniffing
Only bird with whisker-like feathers around its bill
Lays an egg that is 20 percent of its body weight
National symbol of New Zealand
Nocturnal and nearly blind, relying on smell

albatros-hurleur.name: Wandering albatross
descriptions: Largest wingspan of any living bird at 3.5 meters
Can fly thousands of km without flapping its wings
Mates for life with elaborate courtship dances
Spends most of its life at sea without landing
Can live over 60 years in the wild

macareux-moine.name: Atlantic puffin
descriptions: Colorful beak brightens during the breeding season
Can carry dozens of fish crosswise in its beak
Nicknamed the clown of the sea or sea parrot
Nests in burrows on grassy sea cliffs
Flaps wings 400 times per minute in flight

goeland-argente.name: European herring gull
descriptions: Drops shellfish from height to crack them open
Highly adaptable and thrives in urban environments
Can drink both fresh and salt water
Lives in colonies on coasts and rooftops
Recognizes individual humans and remembers faces

sterne-arctique.name: Arctic tern
descriptions: Migrates pole to pole, the longest of any animal
Sees more daylight than any other creature
Travels about 70,000 km annually
Can live over 30 years despite its small size
Breeds in the Arctic and winters in the Antarctic

paon-bleu.name: Indian peafowl
descriptions: Male's tail train can be over 1.5 meters long
Eyespots on tail feathers deter predators
Shakes tail feathers to produce infrasound
National bird of India
Females choose mates based on tail display quality

faisan-dore.name: Golden pheasant
descriptions: Males have golden and red plumage
Native to mountain forests of central China
Can fly short distances but prefers to run
Introduced to many countries as an ornamental bird
Females are plain brown for nesting camouflage

grand-tetras.name: Western capercaillie
descriptions: Largest grouse species in Europe
Males perform dramatic lekking displays at dawn
Makes popping and gurgling sounds during courtship
Eats pine needles and blueberries
Declining across Europe due to habitat loss

perdrix-grise.name: Grey partridge
descriptions: Can lay up to 20 eggs, one of the largest clutches
Lives in open farmland and grassland across Europe
Chicks can run and feed themselves within hours
Population has declined due to modern farming
Forms winter coveys of 10 to 20 birds

dindon-sauvage.name: Wild turkey
descriptions: Ancestor of the domestic turkey
Benjamin Franklin preferred it over the bald eagle
Males gobble to attract females from far away
Can fly short distances at up to 90 km/h
Native to forests of North America

tragopan-satyre.name: Satyr tragopan
descriptions: One of the most colorful pheasants in the world
Male inflates a vivid blue throat lappet in display
Lives in Himalayan forests at high altitudes
Crimson plumage dotted with white pearl-like spots
Nests in trees, unusual for a pheasant

cygne-tubercule.name: Mute swan
descriptions: Can weigh up to 12 kg, one of the heaviest flying birds
Forms a heart shape with its mate during courtship
Fiercely defends its nest from intruders
Orange bill has a distinctive black knob at the base
Royal swans on the Thames belong to the British Crown

canard-colvert.name: Mallard
descriptions: Ancestor of most domestic duck breeds
Males have an iridescent green head
Sleeps with one eye open at the edge of a group
Most widespread duck species in the world
Females quack loudly; males make a softer raspy call

canard-mandarin.name: Mandarin duck
descriptions: Males have multi-colored plumage
Symbol of love and fidelity in East Asian culture
Native to East Asia but established in Europe
Nests in tree holes near water
Chicks jump from the nest hole to the ground at one day old

oie-des-neiges.name: Snow goose
descriptions: Migrates in large noisy V-formations
Can fly at altitudes over 3,000 meters
Has two color forms: white and blue-grey
Population has exploded, damaging Arctic tundra
Breeds in the Canadian Arctic and winters in the US

grue-du-japon.name: Red-crowned crane
descriptions: One of the rarest cranes with about 2,800 left
Sacred in Japan as a symbol of luck and longevity
Performs dancing courtship displays
Stands up to 1.5 meters tall
Mates for life and both parents raise chicks

grue-couronnee.name: Grey crowned crane
descriptions: Has a golden crown of stiff feathers
National bird of Uganda, featured on its flag
Only crane species that can perch in trees
Performs elaborate jumping dances during courtship
Found in wetlands and grasslands of sub-Saharan Africa

toucan-toco.name: Toco toucan
descriptions: Bill is a third of its body length but very light
Bill helps regulate body temperature
Largest toucan species in the world
Tosses fruit into the air and catches it in its bill
Lives in South American tropical forests

calao-rhinoceros.name: Rhinoceros hornbill
descriptions: Has a large horn-like casque on top of its bill
Female seals herself inside a tree hole to nest
Male feeds the female through a narrow slit for months
Found in the rainforests of Southeast Asia
Casque amplifies its calls through the forest

pic-vert.name: European green woodpecker
descriptions: Laughing call is known as the yaffle in Britain
Long sticky tongue wraps around its skull
Feeds mainly on ants extracted from the ground
Undulating flight pattern is distinctive
Found in woodlands and gardens across Europe

pic-epeiche.name: Great spotted woodpecker
descriptions: Most common woodpecker in Europe
Drums on trees at up to 20 strikes per second
Shock-absorbing skull prevents brain injury
Males have a red patch on the back of the head
Tongue can extend 4 cm beyond its bill tip

pigeon-biset.name: Rock dove
descriptions: Ancestor of all domestic pigeon breeds
Can find its way home over hundreds of km
Used to carry messages in both World Wars
One of the first birds domesticated by humans
Can fly at speeds up to 150 km/h

tourterelle-des-bois.name: European turtle dove
descriptions: Purring song is a classic summer sound in Europe
Migrates from Europe to sub-Saharan Africa
Population has declined by 95 percent in decades
Smallest dove native to Europe
Feeds on seeds and grain in open farmland

coucou-gris.name: Common cuckoo
descriptions: Lays its eggs in other birds' nests as a parasite
Chick pushes host eggs out of the nest after hatching
Distinctive 'cuc-koo' call announces spring
Migrates to tropical Africa for winter
Each female mimics eggs of one specific host species

huppe-fasciee.name: Eurasian hoopoe
descriptions: Fan-shaped crest tipped with black
Probes the ground for insects with its curved bill
Makes a soft 'hoo-poo-poo' call giving it its name
Found across Europe, Asia, and Africa
Nest smells terrible as a defense against predators

grebe-huppe.name: Great crested grebe
descriptions: Famous for its elaborate mirrored courtship dance
Pairs present waterweeds to each other during display
Carries chicks on its back while swimming
Can dive underwater for up to 3 minutes
Nearly hunted to extinction for its head plumes

plongeon-huard.name: Common loon
descriptions: Haunting yodel call echoes across northern lakes
Featured on the Canadian one-dollar coin
Can dive to depths of 60 meters for fish
Red eyes help it see underwater
Needs a long runway to take off from water

guepier-d-europe.name: European bee-eater
descriptions: Catches bees and wasps in flight with precision
Rubs prey against a branch to remove the stinger
One of the most colorful birds in Europe
Nests in tunnels dug into sandy banks
Migrates to tropical Africa for winter

rollier-d-europe.name: European roller
descriptions: Named for its rolling flight display
Bright turquoise and blue plumage is unmistakable
Hunts large insects and small reptiles from a perch
Migrates from Europe to southern Africa
Nests in tree holes and old woodpecker cavities

bergeronnette-grise.name: White wagtail
descriptions: Constantly wags its long tail up and down
Found near water, rooftops, and car parks in Europe
Catches insects on the ground with quick dashes
Adapts well to urban environments
Roosts communally in winter in trees or on buildings

alouette-des-champs.name: Eurasian skylark
descriptions: Sings continuously while hovering high in the sky
Flight song can last over 5 minutes nonstop
Nests on the ground in open farmland
Inspired Shelley's famous poem 'To a Skylark'
Population declining due to intensive agriculture

cincle-plongeur.name: White-throated dipper
descriptions: Only songbird that can swim and walk underwater
Hunts aquatic insects on river beds
Bobs up and down on rocks in fast-flowing streams
Has a white breast and chocolate-brown plumage
Can use its wings to 'fly' through the water

jaseur-boreal.name: Bohemian waxwing
descriptions: Silky plumage with red waxy tips on wing feathers
Eats primarily berries and can become intoxicated
Passes berries beak to beak during courtship
Breeds in northern boreal forests of Eurasia
Irrupts south in winter when berry crops fail

loriot-d-europe.name: Eurasian golden oriole
descriptions: Bright yellow and black male is hard to spot in canopy
Fluty song is one of the most beautiful in Europe
Migrates to tropical Africa for winter
Builds a hammock-like nest slung between branches
Rarely descends from the treetops

pie-grieche-ecorcheur.name: Red-backed shrike
descriptions: Impales prey on thorns and barbed wire as a larder
Hunts large insects, lizards, and small birds
Males have a grey head and black bandit mask
Migrates from Europe to southern Africa
Also called the butcher bird for its grisly habit

quetzal-resplendissant.name: Resplendent quetzal
descriptions: Sacred bird of the Aztecs and Mayas
Males have tail feathers up to 65 cm long
Iridescent green plumage shimmers in the light
Lives in cloud forests of Central America
Guatemalan currency is named after this bird

hoatzin-huppe.name: Hoatzin
descriptions: Chicks have claws on their wings for climbing trees
Digests leaves by fermentation like a cow
Also called the stinkbird for its manure-like smell
Found in the Amazon and Orinoco river basins
One of the most primitive living bird species

grue-cendree.name: Common crane
descriptions: One of the most elegant birds in Europe
Performs dancing displays in spring
Migrates in large V-formations across Europe
Trumpeting call can be heard over 2 km away
Stands about 1.2 meters tall

outarde-canepetiere.name: Little bustard
descriptions: Males inflate a black and white neck ruff in display
Lives in open grasslands and steppe in Europe
One of the most threatened birds in Western Europe
Explosive take-off flight with rapid wingbeats
Males make a short rasping call during courtship

heron-garde-boeufs.name: Cattle egret
descriptions: Follows cattle and large mammals to catch stirred-up insects
Originally from Africa, now found on every continent
One of the most successful bird range expansions
Turns orange-buff on head and back during breeding
Roosts in large communal groups at night

butor-etoile.name: Eurasian bittern
descriptions: Booming call can be heard up to 5 km away
Points its bill skyward to mimic reeds for camouflage
Extremely secretive and rarely seen in the open
Lives in dense reed beds across Europe and Asia
Striped brown plumage blends perfectly with reeds

casse-noix-mouchete.name: Spotted nutcracker
descriptions: Buries tens of thousands of pine seeds each autumn
Can remember thousands of cache locations months later
Important for spreading pine trees at high altitudes
Found in mountain conifer forests across Eurasia
Has a strong bill to crack open pine cones

tichodrome-echelette.name: Wallcreeper
descriptions: Climbs vertical cliff faces like a butterfly
Flashes bright crimson wing patches while climbing
One of the most sought-after birds for birdwatchers
Probes cracks in rock faces for insects and spiders
Found on mountain cliffs across southern Eurasia

sitelle-torchepot.name: Eurasian nuthatch
