descriptions: Only European bird that walks headfirst down tree trunks
Plasters mud around nest hole entrance to reduce size
Has a loud, ringing call heard through woodlands
Caches seeds and nuts in bark crevices for winter
Strong feet allow it to cling in any direction

grimpereau-des-jardins.name: Short-toed treecreeper
descriptions: Spirals up tree trunks probing bark for insects
Cryptic brown plumage makes it nearly invisible on bark
Uses its stiff tail as a prop against the trunk
One of the smallest woodland birds in Europe
Thin curved bill extracts insects from bark crevices

rouge-queue-noir.name: Black redstart
descriptions: Vibrates its orange-red tail constantly when perched
Originally a mountain bird that adapted to buildings
Male is dark grey-black with a bright rusty tail
Sings from rooftops very early in the morning
Common in towns and villages across Europe

crocodile-du-nil.name: Nile crocodile
descriptions: Largest reptile in Africa, up to 6 meters long
Bite force of over 22,000 newtons, strongest measured
Can go over a year without eating
Mother carries hatchlings in her jaws to water
Has barely changed in 80 million years

crocodile-marin.name: Saltwater crocodile
descriptions: Largest living reptile, up to 7 meters long
Can swim in open ocean for hundreds of km
Has the strongest bite of any living animal
Found from India to Australia
Can weigh over 1,000 kg

alligator-americain.name: American alligator
descriptions: Can survive freezing by sticking its snout above ice
Was on the brink of extinction but fully recovered
Builds nest mounds of vegetation for its eggs
Males bellow loudly during mating season
Lives in freshwater swamps of the southeastern US

caiman-noir.name: Black caiman
descriptions: Largest member of the alligator family
Can grow up to 5 meters long
Top predator of the Amazon river system
Dark coloring helps it hunt at night
Eats fish, turtles, and even capybaras

gavial-du-gange.name: Gharial
descriptions: Long thin snout is specialized for catching fish
Males have a bulbous growth on the snout tip
Critically endangered with under 650 adults left
Found only in rivers of India and Nepal
Can grow up to 6 meters long

tortue-luth.name: Leatherback sea turtle
descriptions: Largest sea turtle, up to 900 kg
Dives to over 1,200 meters, deepest of any turtle
Has a leathery shell instead of a hard one
Feeds almost exclusively on jellyfish
Migrates over 16,000 km per year

tortue-verte.name: Green sea turtle
descriptions: Named for the green fat under its shell, not its color
One of the largest sea turtles, up to 200 kg
Only herbivorous sea turtle as an adult
Returns to the same beach where it hatched to nest
Can hold its breath for up to 5 hours while sleeping

tortue-imbriquee.name: Hawksbill sea turtle
descriptions: Shell has beautiful overlapping scutes like tiles
Critically endangered, hunted for its shell
Feeds on sponges on coral reefs
Pointed beak reaches into reef crevices for food
Found in tropical oceans worldwide

tortue-caouanne.name: Loggerhead sea turtle
descriptions: Has the largest head of any sea turtle
Powerful jaws crush hard-shelled prey like conchs
Nests on beaches from Florida to the Mediterranean
Can migrate thousands of km across oceans
Hatchlings follow moonlight to find the ocean

tortue-geante-des-galapagos.name: Galápagos giant tortoise
descriptions: Can live over 175 years, longest of any vertebrate
Can weigh up to 400 kg
Helped inspire Darwin's theory of evolution
Each island has a distinct shell shape
Can survive a year without food or water

tortue-geante-d-aldabra.name: Aldabra giant tortoise
descriptions: One of the largest tortoises in the world
Lives on the Aldabra Atoll in the Indian Ocean
Can live over 150 years
Grazes on grass and low plants like a tiny cow
Population is about 100,000 on the remote atoll

tortue-d-hermann.name: Hermann's tortoise
descriptions: One of the most common pet tortoises in Europe
Can live over 100 years in captivity
Native to Mediterranean scrubland and forests
Hibernates during winter months
Shell pattern is unique to each individual

tortue-des-steppes.name: Russian tortoise
descriptions: Also called the Horsfield's tortoise
Lives in arid steppes and deserts of Central Asia
Digs deep burrows to escape extreme temperatures
First tortoise sent into space by the Soviet Union
One of the smallest tortoise species at 15-20 cm

tortue-sulcata.name: African spurred tortoise
descriptions: Third largest tortoise species in the world
Can weigh up to 100 kg as an adult
Lives in the Sahel region south of the Sahara
Digs burrows up to 10 meters long for shelter
Gets most of its water from the plants it eats

tortue-a-tempes-rouges.name: Red-eared slider
descriptions: Most traded reptile in the world as a pet
Named for the red patches behind its eyes
Invasive species in many countries outside the US
Basks in the sun on logs and rocks near water
Can live over 40 years in captivity

tortue-alligator.name: Alligator snapping turtle
descriptions: Largest freshwater turtle in North America
Has a worm-like lure on its tongue to attract fish
Can weigh over 100 kg
Powerful jaws can snap a broomstick in half
Sits motionless on the river bottom waiting for prey

matamata.name: Mata mata
descriptions: Bizarre flat head with skin flaps for camouflage
Looks like a piece of bark or dead leaves
Sucks up prey by rapidly opening its large mouth
Found in slow-moving rivers of South America
Cannot chew; swallows prey whole

python-birman.name: Burmese python
descriptions: One of the largest snakes in the world, up to 7 meters
Invasive in the Florida Everglades
Kills prey by constriction, not venom
Excellent swimmer that can stay submerged 30 minutes
Female coils around eggs and shivers to warm them

anaconda-vert.name: Green anaconda
descriptions: Heaviest snake in the world at up to 250 kg
Can grow over 5 meters long
Semi-aquatic and hunts in rivers and swamps
Eyes and nostrils on top of head for lurking in water
Gives birth to live young, up to 80 at a time

boa-constricteur.name: Boa constrictor
descriptions: Kills prey by constriction, squeezing tighter each breath
Has tiny vestigial legs near its tail
Found from Mexico to Argentina
Gives birth to live young rather than laying eggs
Can sense heat with pits on its lips

cobra-royal.name: King cobra
descriptions: Longest venomous snake, up to 5.5 meters
Can raise a third of its body off the ground
Venom can kill an elephant with one bite
Only snake that builds a nest for its eggs
Growls rather than hisses as a warning

cobra-indien.name: Indian cobra
descriptions: Famous for its expandable hood with eyespot pattern
One of the Big Four snakes causing most snakebites in India
Sacred in Hindu mythology as Naga
Can spit venom up to 2 meters at attackers' eyes
Venom is primarily neurotoxic

mamba-noir.name: Black mamba
descriptions: Fastest snake in the world at up to 20 km/h
Named for the black inside of its mouth, not its color
Venom can kill a human in under an hour untreated
Can strike repeatedly delivering massive doses of venom
Found in savannas and woodlands of sub-Saharan Africa

taipan-du-desert.name: Inland taipan
descriptions: Has the most toxic venom of any land snake
One bite contains enough venom to kill 100 adults
Extremely shy and rarely encountered by humans
Changes color seasonally: darker in winter, lighter in summer
Lives in the remote arid interior of Australia

crotale-diamantin.name: Eastern diamondback rattlesnake
descriptions: Largest rattlesnake species in the world
Rattle is made of interlocking keratin segments
Heat-sensing pits detect warm-blooded prey at night
Fangs fold back against the roof of the mouth
Found in the southeastern United States

vipere-aspic.name: Asp viper
descriptions: Cleopatra reportedly used an asp for her suicide
Found in hilly and mountainous areas of Europe
Turned-up snout tip is a distinguishing feature
Venom is rarely fatal to humans with treatment
Gives birth to live young rather than laying eggs

couleuvre-a-collier.name: Grass snake
descriptions: Plays dead when threatened, rolling onto its back
Named for the yellow and black collar behind its head
Excellent swimmer found near ponds and rivers
Completely harmless to humans
Most widespread snake in Europe

serpent-corail.name: Coral snake
descriptions: Red touches yellow, kill a fellow: a famous rhyme
Has the second most potent venom of any snake
Very shy and rarely bites humans
Bright bands warn predators of its toxicity
Found in forests and deserts of the Americas

serpent-roi-de-californie.name: California kingsnake
descriptions: Immune to rattlesnake venom and eats rattlesnakes
Popular pet snake due to its docile nature
Black and white banded pattern mimics the coral snake
Kills by constriction rather than venom
Found in western North America

dragon-de-komodo.name: Komodo dragon
descriptions: Largest living lizard, up to 3 meters long
Saliva contains venom and toxic bacteria
Can eat up to 80 percent of its body weight in one meal
Excellent swimmer between Indonesian islands
Uses its forked tongue to detect prey from 9 km away

varan-du-nil.name: Nile monitor
descriptions: Largest lizard in Africa, up to 2 meters long
Excellent swimmer and climber
Raids crocodile nests to eat eggs
Can run on its hind legs for short bursts
Revered in ancient Egypt and often mummified

iguane-vert.name: Green iguana
descriptions: Can fall 12 meters from a tree and survive unhurt
Has a third eye on top of its head that senses light
Excellent swimmer using its tail like a rudder
Can grow up to 2 meters including its long tail
Entirely herbivorous as an adult

iguane-marin.name: Marine iguana
descriptions: Only lizard that forages in the ocean
Found only in the Galapagos Islands
Sneezes out excess salt through special glands
Dives up to 12 meters to graze on algae
Huddles in groups to warm up after cold ocean dives

cameleon-panthere.name: Panther chameleon
descriptions: Can change color in seconds for communication
Eyes move independently in different directions
Tongue can extend twice its body length in a fraction of a second
Found only on the island of Madagascar
Males are the most colorful of all chameleons

cameleon-de-jackson.name: Jackson's chameleon
descriptions: Males have three horns like a miniature triceratops
Gives birth to live young instead of laying eggs
Native to the mountains of Kenya and Tanzania
Changes color based on mood and temperature
Prehensile tail grips branches like a fifth limb

gecko-tokay.name: Tokay gecko
descriptions: Named for its loud 'to-kay' call heard at night
One of the largest gecko species at 35 cm
Can walk on smooth vertical surfaces and ceilings
Has a very powerful bite for a lizard its size
Found in Southeast Asia and is often kept in homes

gecko-a-queue-plate.name: Giant Madagascar day gecko
descriptions: Flat tail and body perfectly mimic tree bark
Found only in Madagascar's forests
Nearly invisible when pressed flat against a trunk
Has fringed skin along its body to eliminate shadows
Nocturnal hunter of insects and small invertebrates

lezard-des-murailles.name: Common wall lizard
descriptions: One of the most common lizards in southern Europe
Can shed and regrow its tail to escape predators
Basks on sunny walls, rocks, and ruins
Extremely agile climber on vertical surfaces
Males do push-ups to display dominance

orvet-fragile.name: Slow worm
descriptions: Looks like a snake but is actually a legless lizard
Has eyelids and ear openings, unlike snakes
Can shed its tail when grabbed by a predator
Completely harmless and often found in compost heaps
Can live over 50 years, a record for lizards

scinque-a-langue-bleue.name: Blue-tongued skink
descriptions: Flashes its bright blue tongue to startle predators
One of the largest skink species at up to 60 cm
Popular pet reptile due to its docile nature
Gives birth to live young rather than laying eggs
Native to Australia and nearby islands

basilic-vert.name: Green basilisk
descriptions: Can run across water on its hind legs
Nicknamed the Jesus Christ lizard
Fringed toes trap air pockets for water running
Found in tropical rainforests of Central America
Males have a tall crest along head, back, and tail

moloch-herisse.name: Thorny devil
descriptions: Covered entirely in spiny thorns for defense
Can drink water through its skin from any surface
Changes color to regulate temperature and camouflage
Feeds exclusively on ants, eating thousands per meal
Found only in the deserts of Australia

dragon-barbu.name: Central bearded dragon
descriptions: Puffs out its spiky throat beard when threatened
Waves one arm in a circular motion as a greeting
One of the most popular pet reptiles worldwide
Can change its beard color to black when stressed
Native to the arid regions of Australia

lezard-a-collerette.name: Frilled lizard
descriptions: Unfurls a large frill around its neck when threatened
Runs on its hind legs to escape predators
Frill can be 30 cm in diameter
Found in northern Australia and New Guinea
Spends most of its time in trees

monstre-de-gila.name: Gila monster
descriptions: One of only two venomous lizard species in North America
Venom is delivered through grooved teeth in lower jaw
A compound from its venom is used in diabetes medicine
Can store fat in its thick tail for months
Moves slowly but has a very tenacious bite

tuatara.name: Tuatara
descriptions: Not a lizard; sole survivor of an ancient reptile order
Has a third eye on top of its head
Can live over 100 years
Found only in New Zealand
Thrives at temperatures as low as 5 C, cold for a reptile

vipere-heurtante.name: Puff adder
descriptions: Responsible for the most snakebite deaths in Africa
Has the longest fangs of any viper at up to 5 cm
Strikes extremely fast even from a coiled position
Beautiful geometric pattern provides camouflage in leaf litter
Can inject a very large amount of venom per bite

gecko-leopard.name: Leopard gecko
descriptions: One of the most popular pet reptiles in the world
Has movable eyelids, unlike most gecko species
Cannot climb smooth surfaces as it lacks toe pads
Stores fat in its plump tail for lean times
Native to rocky deserts of Pakistan and India

tortue-serpentine.name: Common snapping turtle
descriptions: Has a powerful bite that can amputate a finger
Cannot fully retract into its shell like most turtles
Algae-covered shell provides excellent camouflage
Found in freshwater habitats across North America
Can weigh up to 35 kg as an adult

couleuvre-d-esculape.name: Aesculapian snake
descriptions: Symbol of medicine on the Rod of Asclepius
One of the longest snakes in Europe at 2 meters
Excellent climber that scales trees and walls
Named after the Greek god of healing
Completely non-venomous and harmless to humans

vipere-peliade.name: Common European adder
descriptions: Only venomous snake found in the British Isles
Lives farther north than any other snake species
Has a distinctive dark zigzag pattern along its back
Bites are painful but rarely fatal to humans
Found across Europe and into northern Asia

serpent-des-bles.name: Corn snake
descriptions: One of the most popular pet snakes in the world
Named for being found in cornfields hunting rodents
Comes in hundreds of color morphs in captivity
Docile temperament makes it ideal for beginners
Native to the southeastern United States

crocodile-du-nil-nain.name: Dwarf crocodile
descriptions: Also known as the West African dwarf crocodile
Smallest crocodile species at about 1.5 meters
Nocturnal and very shy compared to other crocs
Lives in forests and swamps of West Africa
Digs burrows in riverbanks for shelter

varan-de-salvador.name: Crocodile monitor
descriptions: Also called the crocodile monitor for its long tail
Can grow over 2.5 meters long, mostly tail
Found only in the forests of Papua New Guinea
Has a very long neck relative to other monitors
Arboreal lizard that hunts in the forest canopy

lezard-vert-occidental.name: Western green lizard
descriptions: Vivid bright green coloring with blue throat in males
Found in Western Europe in sunny bushy habitats
Can grow up to 40 cm including tail
Hunts large insects, snails, and small lizards
Males fight by biting each other during breeding season

tortue-cistude.name: European pond turtle
descriptions: Only native freshwater turtle of much of Europe
Yellow spots on dark shell and skin are distinctive
Basks on logs and rocks near ponds and marshes
Can live over 60 years in the wild
Declining due to habitat loss and invasive species

python-vert.name: Green tree python
descriptions: Brilliant emerald green coloring as an adult
Juveniles can be bright yellow, red, or brown
Lives in the rainforests of Australia and New Guinea
Ambushes prey from coiled positions in tree branches
Has deep heat-sensing pits along its lips

anolis-vert.name: Carolina anole
descriptions: Can change color from bright green to dark brown
Males display a bright pink-red throat fan called a dewlap
Sometimes called the American chameleon
Found in the southeastern United States
Has adhesive toe pads for climbing smooth surfaces

grand-requin-blanc.name: Great white shark
descriptions: Can detect one drop of blood in 100 liters of water
Has about 300 serrated teeth in multiple rows
Can breach fully out of the water when attacking
Lives up to 70 years or more
Body temperature is warmer than surrounding water

requin-baleine.name: Whale shark
descriptions: Largest fish in the world at up to 18 meters
Gentle filter feeder that eats plankton and small fish
Each individual has a unique spot pattern
Mouth can be over 1.5 meters wide
Despite its size, completely harmless to humans

requin-marteau.name: Great hammerhead shark
descriptions: Wide head provides 360-degree vertical vision
Head shape helps detect prey buried in sand
Schools of hundreds have been observed at seamounts
Uses its head to pin stingrays to the ocean floor
Found in warm temperate and tropical oceans

requin-tigre.name: Tiger shark
descriptions: Named for dark stripes on its body as a juvenile
Eats almost anything including license plates and tires
Known as the garbage can of the sea
Has uniquely shaped teeth for cutting through shells
Found in tropical and warm temperate waters

requin-bleu.name: Blue shark
descriptions: Most widespread shark species in the world
Can migrate over 9,000 km in a single journey
Distinctive deep blue color on its back
Slender body built for speed and long-distance travel
Gives birth to up to 135 pups in one litter

requin-mako.name: Shortfin mako shark
descriptions: Fastest shark in the ocean at over 70 km/h
Can leap up to 6 meters out of the water
Streamlined body is built for speed
One of the few sharks dangerous to humans
Close relative of the great white shark

requin-pelerin.name: Basking shark
descriptions: Second largest fish in the world after whale shark
Filters over 2,000 tonnes of water per hour
Mouth opens to nearly 1 meter wide while feeding
Despite huge size, feeds on tiny plankton
Found in temperate oceans worldwide

requin-renard.name: Common thresher shark
descriptions: Tail is as long as its body, used to stun prey
Whips its tail like a weapon to stun fish schools
Can leap fully out of the water
Found in open oceans worldwide
Relatively harmless to humans despite its size

requin-taureau.name: Sand tiger shark
descriptions: Can survive in both salt and fresh water
Found in rivers hundreds of km from the ocean
One of the most dangerous sharks to humans
Stocky build and aggressive temperament
Has the strongest bite force of any shark species

requin-citron.name: Lemon shark
descriptions: Named for its yellowish-brown skin color
Can rest motionless on the ocean floor unlike most sharks
One of the best-studied shark species
Found in shallow subtropical waters of the Americas
Forms social groups and returns to birthplace to breed

requin-de-recif.name: Blacktip reef shark
descriptions: Most common shark on tropical coral reefs
Active nocturnal hunter of reef fish
Can be identified by black tips on its fins
Important for maintaining healthy reef ecosystems
Generally shy around humans and divers

ange-de-mer.name: Common angel shark
descriptions: Flat body shape makes it look like a ray
Buries itself in sand to ambush passing prey
Was once common but is now critically endangered
Strikes prey in a tenth of a second
Found on sandy bottoms of coastal waters

raie-manta.name: Giant oceanic manta ray
descriptions: Largest ray species with wingspan up to 7 meters
Has the largest brain of any fish species
Recognized individual mantas show self-awareness
Filter feeds on plankton and small fish
Can leap fully out of the water

raie-pastenague.name: Common stingray
descriptions: Has a venomous barbed stinger on its tail
Buries itself in sand with only its eyes exposed
Found in shallow coastal waters worldwide
Shuffling feet in sand alerts rays to avoid stings
Some species can live in fresh water

raie-torpille.name: Marbled electric ray
descriptions: Generates electric shocks of up to 220 volts
Uses electricity to stun prey and deter predators
Was used in ancient Rome as pain relief therapy
Round flat body with two electric organs
Found in temperate and tropical seas worldwide

poisson-scie.name: Sawfish
descriptions: Long saw-like snout has electroreceptors for hunting
Slashes its saw through fish schools to stun prey
Critically endangered; all species are at risk
Can grow up to 7 meters long
Related to rays despite looking like sharks

thon-rouge.name: Atlantic bluefin tuna
descriptions: Can swim at speeds up to 70 km/h
Warm-blooded, rare for a fish
A single fish sold for 3 million USD at auction
Can cross the Atlantic Ocean in under 60 days
Can weigh over 600 kg and live 40 years

espadon.name: Swordfish
descriptions: Long flat bill is used to slash and stun prey
Can swim at speeds up to 97 km/h
One of the fastest fish in the ocean
Has a special organ to heat its brain and eyes
Loses all teeth and scales as an adult

marlin-bleu.name: Atlantic blue marlin
descriptions: Can weigh over 800 kg, a prized game fish
Changes color rapidly from blue to silver when excited
Uses its spear-like bill to stun schools of fish
Can swim at bursts over 110 km/h
Made famous by Hemingway's The Old Man and the Sea

poisson-lune.name: Ocean sunfish
descriptions: Heaviest bony fish in the world at up to 2,300 kg
Looks like a giant swimming head with no tail
Lays more eggs than any vertebrate: 300 million
Basks on its side at the surface to warm up
Feeds mainly on jellyfish and needs lots to survive

barracuda.name: Great barracuda
descriptions: Has fang-like teeth and a fearsome appearance
Can accelerate to 58 km/h in a short burst
Attracted to shiny objects which can look like fish scales
Found in tropical and subtropical oceans
Hunts using surprise attacks from ambush

maquereau-commun.name: Atlantic mackerel
descriptions: Swims in large schools for protection from predators
Has no swim bladder so must keep swimming to stay afloat
Distinctive wavy pattern of dark bars on its back
One of the most commercially important fish species
Can swim at speeds up to 25 km/h

poisson-clown.name: Clownfish
descriptions: Lives among venomous anemone tentacles unharmed
Mucus coating protects it from anemone stings
All are born male; dominant fish becomes female
Made famous by the film Finding Nemo
Rarely ventures more than a meter from its anemone

poisson-chirurgien-bleu.name: Blue tang
descriptions: Has a sharp spine near its tail like a surgeon's scalpel
Bright blue color fades to dark at night
Made famous as Dory in Finding Nemo
Grazes on algae, keeping coral reefs healthy
Found in coral reefs of the Indo-Pacific

poisson-ange-empereur.name: Emperor angelfish
descriptions: Juveniles have a completely different pattern than adults
Brilliant blue and yellow stripes as an adult
Found on coral reefs of the Indo-Pacific
Color change from juvenile to adult takes years
Can live up to 20 years on the reef

poisson-papillon.name: Pennant coralfish
descriptions: Has a false eyespot near its tail to confuse predators
Many species mate for life and pair together
Found on coral reefs in tropical oceans
Long snout probes into crevices for food
Over 100 species exist in a rainbow of colors

poisson-napoleon.name: Humphead wrasse
descriptions: Largest wrasse species at up to 2 meters
Named for the hump on its head resembling a hat
Can live over 30 years on coral reefs
Can eat toxic animals like sea hares and starfish
Endangered due to overfishing in Southeast Asia

labre-nettoyeur.name: Bluestreak cleaner wrasse
descriptions: Runs cleaning stations where it removes fish parasites
Larger fish queue patiently for their turn to be cleaned
Can recognize itself in a mirror, a sign of intelligence
Only about 10 cm long but serves vital reef role
Found on coral reefs throughout the Indo-Pacific

merou-geant.name: Giant grouper
descriptions: Can grow up to 2.7 meters and weigh 400 kg
Swallows prey whole with a powerful suction gulp
Solitary and territorial on its section of reef
Can live over 50 years
Boom sound it makes can be felt in a diver's chest

poisson-globe.name: Pufferfish
descriptions: Inflates into a spiky ball when threatened
Contains tetrodotoxin, one of nature's deadliest poisons
Considered a delicacy in Japan as fugu
Chefs need a special license to prepare it safely
Some species create intricate sand circles for courtship

poisson-coffre.name: Yellow boxfish
descriptions: Has a rigid bony shell covering most of its body
Releases a toxin into water when stressed
Swims using only its small fins, not body movement
Box shape inspired a concept car by Mercedes-Benz
Found on coral reefs in tropical waters

murene-verte.name: Green moray
descriptions: Has a second set of jaws in its throat to pull in prey
Green color comes from yellow mucus over blue skin
Can grow up to 2.5 meters long
Hides in reef crevices with only its head visible
Often opens and closes its mouth to breathe, not threaten

brochet.name: Northern pike
descriptions: Top freshwater predator in European and North American lakes
Can strike at prey with explosive speed from ambush
Has over 700 razor-sharp teeth
Can grow up to 1.5 meters and weigh 25 kg
Called the water wolf for its ferocious hunting style

truite-fario.name: Brown trout
descriptions: Requires clean cold water to survive
Red and black spots make it one of the prettiest fish
An indicator species for water quality
Can live over 20 years in ideal conditions
Native to European rivers and streams

saumon-atlantique.name: Atlantic salmon
descriptions: Returns to its birth river to spawn using smell
Can leap up waterfalls over 3 meters high
Changes color from silver to red during spawning
One of the most commercially valuable fish species
Unlike Pacific salmon, can survive spawning to breed again

perche-du-nil.name: Nile perch
descriptions: One of the largest freshwater fish at up to 200 kg
Introduced to Lake Victoria, devastating native species
Important commercially but ecologically destructive
Can grow up to 2 meters long
Native to rivers and lakes across Africa

silure-glane.name: Wels catfish
descriptions: Largest freshwater fish in Europe at up to 2.7 meters
Has been filmed lunging onto shore to catch pigeons
Six long barbels help it sense prey in murky water
Can live over 50 years
Active primarily at night

piranha-rouge.name: Red-bellied piranha
descriptions: Reputation as a ferocious killer is mostly exaggerated
Has razor-sharp interlocking teeth
Feeds mainly on fish, insects, and plants
Can strip flesh quickly in a feeding frenzy
Found in rivers of South America

arowana-asiatique.name: Asian arowana
descriptions: Called the dragon fish and prized as a luck symbol
Can sell for over 300,000 USD in the aquarium trade
Leaps out of water to catch insects and birds
Endangered in the wild due to overcollection
Male broods eggs and fry in its mouth

discus.name: Discus
descriptions: Called the king of the aquarium for its beauty
Round flat body shaped like a disc
Parents secrete nutritious mucus for fry to feed on
Found in calm backwaters of the Amazon
Requires very specific water conditions to thrive

hippocampe-commun.name: Short-snouted seahorse
descriptions: Male carries and gives birth to the babies
Has no stomach so must eat almost constantly
Grasps objects with its prehensile tail
Eyes move independently like a chameleon
Can change color to match surroundings

dragon-de-mer-feuillu.name: Leafy seadragon
descriptions: Leaf-like appendages provide perfect camouflage
Found only off the coast of southern Australia
Moves so slowly it appears to drift like seaweed
Male carries eggs on a brood patch under its tail
Marine emblem of the state of South Australia

poisson-lanterne.name: Lanternfish
descriptions: Produces its own light through bioluminescence
Lives in the deep ocean at 200 to 1,000 meters
One of the most abundant fish in the deep sea
Migrates to surface at night to feed on plankton
Light organs help it attract mates and confuse predators

coelacanthe.name: Coelacanth
descriptions: Thought extinct for 66 million years until found in 1938
Called a living fossil for its ancient lineage
Has lobed fins that move like four-legged animals
Lives at depths of 150 to 700 meters
Can live up to 100 years

anguille-d-europe.name: European eel
descriptions: Migrates over 5,000 km to the Sargasso Sea to breed
No one has ever observed eels mating in the wild
Changes form multiple times during its life cycle
Can cross short stretches of land on wet grass
Critically endangered due to overfishing and dams

esturgeon-d-europe.name: European sturgeon
descriptions: One of the oldest fish lineages at 200 million years
Can grow over 5 meters long and weigh 300 kg
Source of caviar, leading to severe overfishing
Critically endangered in European rivers
Has bony plates called scutes instead of scales

poisson-archer.name: Archerfish
descriptions: Shoots jets of water to knock insects off branches
Can hit targets up to 2 meters above the water
Compensates for light refraction when aiming
Found in mangroves and estuaries of Southeast Asia
Learns and improves accuracy with practice

gymnote-electrique.name: Electric eel
descriptions: Can generate shocks of up to 860 volts
Not a true eel but a type of knifefish
Uses electric fields to navigate in murky water
Can remotely control prey muscles with its discharge
Found in the rivers of South America

poisson-volant.name: Flying fish
descriptions: Glides above the ocean surface for up to 200 meters
Can reach speeds of 70 km/h before launching
Uses enlarged pectoral fins as wings
Glides to escape predators like tuna and dolphins
Found in warm tropical and subtropical oceans

baudroie-commune.name: Anglerfish
descriptions: Uses a bioluminescent lure to attract prey in the dark
Female can be 10 times larger than the male
Males fuse to the female's body permanently in some species
Has an enormous mouth for swallowing large prey
Lives on the ocean floor at great depths

carpe-commune.name: Common carp
descriptions: Domesticated in China over 2,000 years ago
Can live over 100 years in ideal conditions
Has barbels around its mouth for sensing food
Considered invasive in many countries worldwide
Koi are a colorful domesticated variety of this fish

poisson-chat-d-europe.name: American catfish
descriptions: Has long whisker-like barbels for sensing prey
Can survive in low-oxygen waters
Active mainly at night, hiding by day
Found in slow rivers and lakes across Europe
Can deliver a mildly venomous sting from its spines

sandre.name: Pike-perch
descriptions: Highly prized game and food fish in Europe
Has large canine-like teeth for catching fish
Prefers murky turbid waters where it has an advantage
Eyes have a reflective layer for excellent night vision
Native to Eastern Europe but widely introduced

perche-commune.name: European perch
descriptions: Has distinctive dark vertical bars on a green body
Red-orange pelvic and anal fins are striking
One of the most widespread freshwater fish in Europe
Hunts in small packs for greater success
Spiny dorsal fin deters many predators

ombre-commun.name: European grayling
descriptions: Has a large colorful sail-like dorsal fin
Smells faintly of thyme when freshly caught
Requires clean cold rivers to thrive
Found across Europe in fast-flowing waters
An indicator of excellent water quality

gardon.name: Common roach
descriptions: One of the most common freshwater fish in Europe
Silvery body with distinctive red eyes and fins
Lives in schools in lakes, ponds, and slow rivers
Important prey species for pike and perch
Tolerates a wide range of water conditions

tanche.name: Tench
descriptions: Called the doctor fish; its slime was thought to heal
Thick slimy skin protects it from parasites
Olive-green body with small scales deeply embedded
Thrives in warm weedy lakes and ponds
Can survive in waters with very low oxygen

bar-commun.name: European seabass
descriptions: Prized by European anglers as a sport fish
Hunts in surf zones along rocky coasts
Silvery body with a distinctive dark back
Can live up to 30 years in the wild
Feeds on crabs, shrimps, and small fish

sole-commune.name: Common sole
descriptions: Both eyes migrate to one side as it develops
Lies flat on the seabed perfectly camouflaged
Considered one of the finest eating fish in Europe
Hunts at night using sensitive barbels to find prey
Can change skin color to match the sea floor

cabillaud.name: Atlantic cod
descriptions: Once so abundant it shaped North Atlantic economies
Can live up to 25 years and weigh over 50 kg
Has a distinctive barbel on its chin
Overfishing caused the famous cod collapse in the 1990s
Found in cold waters of the North Atlantic

sardine.name: European pilchard
descriptions: Swims in massive schools of millions for protection
Named after the island of Sardinia
One of the most important commercial fish worldwide
Rich in omega-3 fatty acids
Migrates in shoals off the coast of South Africa

hareng-atlantique.name: Atlantic herring
descriptions: Has been a vital food fish for over a thousand years
Schools can number in the billions
Communicates by releasing bubbles from its swim bladder
Found throughout the North Atlantic
Herring wars shaped European history for centuries

requin-dormeur.name: Nurse shark
descriptions: Rests motionless on the sea floor during the day
Active nocturnal hunter of sea urchins and crabs
Has a blunt head and crushing teeth
Found in the Pacific Ocean along the Americas
Harmless to humans despite its stocky appearance

poisson-scorpion.name: Red lionfish
descriptions: Master of camouflage on the ocean floor
Venomous spines can cause extremely painful stings
Ambush predator that strikes in milliseconds
Found in tropical and temperate oceans
Nearly impossible to spot among rocks and coral

poisson-pierre.name: Stonefish
descriptions: Most venomous fish in the world
Looks exactly like a rock on the sea floor
Sting can be fatal to humans without treatment
Strikes prey in just 0.015 seconds
Found in the shallow waters of the Indo-Pacific

turbot.name: Turbot
descriptions: Diamond-shaped flat body with bony tubercles
Highly prized as one of the finest eating fish
Can change color to match the sea floor
Ambush predator that lunges at passing fish
Found on sandy and muddy bottoms in European waters

raie-bouclee.name: Thornback ray
descriptions: Named for rows of thorny bucklers on its back
Most common ray species in European waters
Lays egg cases called mermaid's purses
Uses its flat body to pin prey on the seabed
Can grow up to 1.2 meters in wingspan

lotte.name: Burbot
descriptions: Has a large flat head and enormous mouth
Only freshwater fish in the cod family
Found in cold deep lakes and rivers across the north
Active primarily in winter under ice
Considered a delicacy in many northern European countries

omble-chevalier.name: Arctic char
descriptions: Lives in the coldest and deepest lakes in the world
Northernmost freshwater fish species on Earth
Developed many isolated lake-dwelling forms
Vivid red belly during breeding season
Close relative of trout and salmon

ablette.name: Common bleak
descriptions: Silvery scales were once used to make artificial pearls
Small schooling fish found across European rivers
Surface feeder that eats insects and plankton
Rarely exceeds 20 cm in length
Popular bait fish for anglers targeting larger species

papillon-monarque.name: Monarch butterfly
descriptions: Migrates up to 4,800 km from Canada to Mexico
Millions gather on trees in Mexico each winter
Toxic from eating milkweed as a caterpillar
Bright orange warns predators of its toxicity
No single butterfly completes the full round trip

morpho-bleu.name: Blue morpho
descriptions: Wings are not blue; microscopic scales reflect blue light
Underside is brown with eyespots for camouflage
Wingspan reaches up to 20 cm
Found in the tropical rainforests of Central and South America
Iridescent color inspired anti-counterfeiting technology

machaon.name: Old World swallowtail
descriptions: Named after a surgeon from Greek mythology
Caterpillar has an orange forked scent organ for defense
Wingspan can reach 10 cm in some subspecies
Found across Europe, Asia, and North America
Has distinctive tail-like extensions on its hind wings

vulcain.name: Red admiral
descriptions: Migrates from North Africa to Europe each spring
Bold red and black wings are unmistakable
One of the last butterflies to be seen in autumn
Feeds on rotting fruit and tree sap
Can fly at speeds up to 30 km/h

paon-du-jour.name: European peacock butterfly
descriptions: Four large eyespots on its wings deter predators
Hisses by rubbing its wings together when threatened
One of the most common butterflies in Europe
Overwinters as an adult in sheds and hollow trees
Caterpillars feed on stinging nettles

aurore.name: Orange tip
descriptions: Males have bright orange wing tips; females are white
One of the first butterflies to appear in spring
Caterpillar feeds on garlic mustard and cuckoo flower
Found across Europe and temperate Asia
Wingspan of about 4 to 5 cm

citron.name: Common brimstone
descriptions: Can live up to 13 months, longest of any butterfly
Leaf-shaped wings provide excellent camouflage
Males are bright yellow; females are pale greenish
Hibernates through winter and flies again in spring
One of the first butterflies to appear each year

flambe.name: Scarce swallowtail
descriptions: Pale wings with dark tiger stripes and long tails
Soars and glides rather than fluttering like most butterflies
Found in warm orchards and gardens across southern Europe
Caterpillar feeds on blackthorn and fruit trees
Wingspan reaches up to 8 cm

ornithoptere-de-la-reine-alexandra.name: Queen Alexandra's birdwing
descriptions: Largest butterfly in the world with 31 cm wingspan
Found only in Papua New Guinea's rainforests
Critically endangered by habitat destruction
Males are blue-green; females are brown and larger
Named after Queen Alexandra of the UK

bombyx-du-murier.name: Silkworm moth
descriptions: Source of all commercial silk for over 5,000 years
Fully domesticated and cannot survive in the wild
Has lost the ability to fly
Each cocoon is made of a single silk thread up to 900 m long
Caterpillar eats exclusively mulberry leaves

sphinx-tete-de-mort.name: Death's-head hawkmoth
descriptions: Has a skull-shaped marking on its thorax
Can squeak loudly when disturbed
Raids beehives for honey and is immune to stings
One of the largest moths in Europe
Featured in the film Silence of the Lambs

moro-sphinx.name: Hummingbird hawk-moth
descriptions: Hovers like a hummingbird while feeding on flowers
Wings beat up to 85 times per second
Can fly at speeds up to 45 km/h
Migrates from North Africa to northern Europe
Also called the hummingbird hawk-moth

grand-mars-changeant.name: Purple emperor
descriptions: Wings shimmer with purple iridescence in sunlight
Males are attracted to smelly substances on the ground
Feeds on tree sap, dung, and rotting fruit, not flowers
Found in deciduous forests across Europe
Caterpillar feeds on willow and poplar leaves

tabac-d-espagne.name: Silver-washed fritillary
descriptions: Largest fritillary butterfly in Europe
Males have distinctive dark scent lines on wings
Lays eggs near but not on violet plants for caterpillars
Bright orange upper wings with dark spotted pattern
Found in woodland clearings across Europe and Asia

scarabee-sacre.name: Sacred scarab
descriptions: Rolls dung into perfect balls for its larvae to eat
Sacred symbol in ancient Egypt representing the sun god
Navigates using the Milky Way as a compass
Can move dung balls 10 times its own weight
One of the few insects known to use celestial navigation

lucane-cerf-volant.name: European stag beetle
descriptions: Largest beetle in Europe at up to 9 cm
Males use huge antler-like mandibles to fight rivals
Larvae live in decaying wood for up to 5 years
Adults live only a few weeks to reproduce
Can fly despite its heavy appearance

dynaste-hercule.name: Hercules beetle
descriptions: One of the largest beetles in the world at 17 cm
Can lift 850 times its own body weight
Males have a massive horn on their head and thorax
Found in Central and South American rainforests
Elytra change color based on humidity

coccinelle-a-sept-points.name: Seven-spot ladybird
descriptions: Eats up to 5,000 aphids in its lifetime
Bright red color warns predators of its bitter taste
Bleeds toxic yellow fluid from its knees when threatened
Seven spots is the most common pattern in Europe
Considered a symbol of good luck in many cultures

hanneton-commun.name: Common cockchafer
descriptions: Larvae spend 3 to 4 years underground eating roots
Adults emerge in May and fly clumsily at dusk
Was once so common that children collected them as toys
Population has declined dramatically due to pesticides
Antennae have fan-like plates that detect scents

carabe-dore.name: Golden ground beetle
descriptions: Brilliant metallic golden-green coloring
Voracious predator of slugs and snails in gardens
Cannot fly as its wing covers are fused shut
Squirts foul-smelling liquid at attackers
One of the most beneficial insects for gardeners

ver-luisant.name: Common glow-worm
descriptions: Female glows green at night to attract flying males
Light is produced by a chemical reaction with near 100 percent efficiency
Males can fly but females are wingless
Not a worm but actually a beetle
Larvae eat slugs and snails

capricorne-des-maisons.name: House longhorn beetle
descriptions: Larvae bore into softwood timber in buildings
Can cause serious structural damage to houses
Larvae can live inside wood for over 10 years
Adults are grey-brown with long curved antennae
One of the most destructive wood-boring insects

doryphore.name: Colorado potato beetle
descriptions: Most destructive potato pest in the world
Distinctive yellow and black striped wing covers
Can develop resistance to pesticides rapidly
Female lays up to 800 eggs in a season
Native to Colorado but has spread worldwide

charancon-rouge-du-palmier.name: Red palm weevil
descriptions: One of the most damaging pests to palm trees
Larvae bore through the trunk destroying the tree
Adults are attracted by the smell of damaged palms
Invasive species spreading across the Mediterranean
Can kill a palm tree in just a few months

titan.name: Titan beetle
descriptions: One of the largest beetles in the world at 17 cm
Mandibles can snap a pencil in half
Adults do not eat and live only to reproduce
Found in the Amazon rainforest
Larvae have never been found in the wild

abeille-domestique.name: Western honey bee
descriptions: Visits up to 5,000 flowers in a single day
Communicates flower locations with a waggle dance
A colony can produce 30 kg of honey per year
Queen can lay up to 2,000 eggs per day
Responsible for pollinating a third of our food crops

bourdon-terrestre.name: Buff-tailed bumblebee
descriptions: Can fly in temperatures too cold for most insects
Vibrates its muscles to warm up before flight
Buzz pollinates tomatoes and blueberries effectively
Queen hibernates alone underground all winter
Can sting multiple times unlike honey bees

frelon-europeen.name: European hornet
descriptions: Largest wasp species in Europe at up to 3.5 cm
Hunts other insects including large moths and wasps
Less aggressive toward humans than common wasps
Attracted to light at night unlike most wasps
Builds papery nests in hollow trees and attics

frelon-asiatique.name: Asian hornet
descriptions: Invasive species devastating European honey bee colonies
Hovers outside hives to catch returning worker bees
Originally from Southeast Asia, arrived in France in 2004
Can destroy a bee colony in just a few hours
Slightly smaller than the European hornet

fourmi-rousse-des-bois.name: Red wood ant
descriptions: Builds huge dome-shaped mounds of pine needles
Colonies can contain over 300,000 workers
Sprays formic acid at predators in defense
Controls pest insects in the forest
Can carry objects 50 times their own weight

fourmi-champignonniste.name: Leafcutter ant
descriptions: Farms its own food by growing fungus on cut leaves
Colony structure is one of the most complex in nature
Workers cut and carry leaf pieces many times their weight
Has been farming for over 50 million years
Found in tropical forests of the Americas

fourmi-de-feu.name: Red imported fire ant
descriptions: Sting feels like being burned, giving it its name
Forms living rafts to survive floods by linking together
One of the most invasive species in the world
Colony can have multiple queens with millions of workers
Native to South America but now found on every continent

abeille-coucou.name: Carpenter bee
descriptions: Lays its eggs in the nests of other bee species
Lacks pollen-collecting structures like other bees
Kills or evicts the host bee's eggs
Named for its parasitic behavior like cuckoo birds
Thicker exoskeleton protects it from host bee attacks

libellule-deprimee.name: Broad-bodied chaser
descriptions: Males have a distinctive powder-blue flattened abdomen
Can fly at speeds up to 30 km/h
Catches insects in flight with basket-shaped legs
Common near ponds and lakes across Europe
Was one of the first dragonfly species described in science

anax-empereur.name: Emperor dragonfly
descriptions: One of the largest dragonflies in Europe at 78 mm
Males are bright blue; females are green
Can catch prey as large as butterflies in flight
Patrols a territory over water, chasing all rivals
Larvae are fierce aquatic predators for up to 2 years

calopteryx-eclatant.name: Beautiful demoiselle
descriptions: Males have iridescent blue-green wings
Performs a fluttering courtship display over streams
Found along clean fast-flowing rivers and streams
An indicator of good water quality
Wings appear to flash as it flies in dappled sunlight

demoiselle.name: Azure damselfly
descriptions: Delicate damselfly with metallic colored body
Holds wings folded over body, unlike dragonflies
Found near slow-moving water across Europe
Males display by opening and closing their colored wings
Larvae are slender aquatic predators

mante-religieuse.name: European mantis
descriptions: Female sometimes eats the male during mating
Can turn its head 180 degrees to scan surroundings
Strikes prey in less than a tenth of a second
Only insect that can look over its own shoulder
Named for its prayer-like resting pose

mante-orchidee.name: Orchid mantis
descriptions: Mimics a pink orchid flower to ambush pollinators
One of the most beautiful insect mimics in nature
Legs resemble flower petals
Attracts more insects than actual flowers nearby
Found in the tropical forests of Southeast Asia

mante-feuille-morte.name: Dead leaf mantis
descriptions: Mimics a dead brown leaf perfectly for camouflage
Stays motionless for hours waiting for prey
Even has markings that look like leaf veins and spots
Found in the forests of Southeast Asia
Virtually invisible on the forest floor

phasme-baton.name: Common walking stick
descriptions: Looks exactly like a thin twig or stick
Can regenerate lost legs after molting
Sways gently to mimic a branch in the wind
Some species can reproduce without males
One of the most popular pet insects worldwide

phasme-feuille.name: Leaf insect
descriptions: Mimics a green leaf so perfectly it even has fake veins
Rocks side to side like a leaf in the breeze
Found in the tropical forests of Southeast Asia
Even eggs look like plant seeds
Among the best-camouflaged insects

criquet-pelerin.name: Desert locust
descriptions: Forms devastating swarms of billions covering the sky
A single swarm can eat as much food as 35,000 people
Changes color and behavior when forming a swarm
Can travel 150 km per day in a swarm
Has plagued humanity since ancient times

grillon-champetre.name: Field cricket
descriptions: Chirps by rubbing its wings together
Chirping rate increases with temperature
Lives in burrows in grasslands and meadows
Males chirp to attract females and warn rivals
Can jump 20 to 30 times its body length

sauterelle-verte.name: Great green bush-cricket
descriptions: One of the largest insects in Europe at 6 cm
Has a powerful bite that can break human skin
Can fly and leap great distances
Produces a loud stridulating song in late summer
Hunts other insects as well as eating plants

weta-geant.name: Giant weta
descriptions: One of the heaviest insects in the world at 70 g
Found only in New Zealand
Has barely changed in 190 million years
Too heavy to fly or even jump
Name means 'god of ugly things' in Maori

mouche-domestique.name: House fly
descriptions: Can taste food with its feet
Eyes have 4,000 individual lenses each
Beats its wings about 200 times per second
Can walk upside down using sticky pads on its feet
Life span is only about 28 days

moustique-tigre.name: Asian tiger mosquito
descriptions: Black and white striped body gives it its name
Invasive species spreading diseases worldwide
Only females bite; they need blood for egg production
Can breed in a bottle cap of standing water
Transmits dengue, chikungunya, and Zika viruses

syrphe-ceinture.name: Marmalade hoverfly
descriptions: Mimics a wasp but is completely harmless
Important pollinator of flowers and crops
Can hover motionless in the air like a helicopter
Larvae eat aphids, making them useful for pest control
Found in gardens and meadows across Europe

cigale-commune.name: Common cicada
descriptions: Males produce the loudest sound of any insect
Song can reach 120 decibels, as loud as a chainsaw
Nymphs live underground for several years
Sound is produced by vibrating membranes called tymbals
Symbol of the south of France and Mediterranean summer

punaise-verte.name: Southern green stink bug
descriptions: Releases a foul-smelling chemical when threatened
Also called a stink bug for its strong odor
Changes color from green in summer to brown in autumn
Found on plants in gardens and orchards across Europe
Feeds by piercing plants and sucking their sap

gerris.name: Common water strider
descriptions: Walks on water using surface tension and long legs
Tiny hairs on its legs trap air for buoyancy
Detects prey by sensing vibrations on the water surface
Also called a water strider or pond skater
Found on still and slow-moving fresh water worldwide

puceron-vert-du-rosier.name: Green rose aphid
descriptions: Reproduces explosively fast; females give live birth
Can produce clones without mating in summer
Major pest of roses and garden plants
Excretes honeydew that ants farm and protect them for
Tiny at just 2 mm but occurs in vast numbers

perce-oreille-commun.name: Common earwig
descriptions: Pincers on its rear end are used for defense and mating
Despite its name, it does not enter human ears
Mother earwig guards and cleans her eggs diligently
Nocturnal and hides in dark crevices by day
Can fly but rarely does

termite-souterrain.name: Subterranean termite
descriptions: Colonies can contain millions of individuals
Causes billions of dollars in damage worldwide annually
Queen can live over 25 years and lay thousands of eggs daily
Workers are blind and communicate through chemicals
Digests wood using symbiotic microbes in its gut

bousier-sacre.name: Sacred dung beetle
descriptions: Rolls dung balls across the ground with its hind legs
Uses the Milky Way and moonlight for navigation
Recycles nutrients back into the soil
Male and female cooperate to bury dung balls
Worshipped in ancient Egypt as a sacred symbol

cerf-volant-geant.name: Giraffe stag beetle
descriptions: One of the largest stag beetles in the world
Males use enormous mandibles in wrestling matches
Found in the tropical forests of Southeast Asia
Larvae feed on rotting wood for several years
Can fly despite looking too heavy for its wings

chrysomele-du-peuplier.name: Poplar leaf beetle
descriptions: Bright red or orange with black spots on its elytra
Feeds on poplar and willow leaves
Larvae exude a foul-smelling defensive secretion
Can defoliate entire trees in large numbers
Found across Europe and parts of Asia

belle-dame.name: Painted lady
descriptions: Migrates from Africa to northern Europe each year
One of the most widespread butterflies in the world
Cannot survive European winters; migrates south each autumn
Also called the painted lady butterfly
Can cover thousands of kilometers during migration

demi-deuil.name: Marbled white
descriptions: Distinctive black and white checkered wing pattern
Name means half-mourning in French for its colors
Common in meadows and grasslands of Europe
Flies in a slow bouncing manner close to the ground
Caterpillars feed on various grasses

petite-tortue.name: Small tortoiseshell
descriptions: Named for the tortoiseshell pattern on its wings
One of the most common European garden butterflies
Hibernates indoors in attics and sheds over winter
Blue spots along wing edges flash when wings open
Caterpillars feed on stinging nettles

pieride-du-chou.name: Large white butterfly
descriptions: One of the most common butterflies in Europe
Caterpillars are a major pest of cabbage crops
White wings with black tips are easily recognized
Migrates in large numbers across the English Channel
Has been accidentally introduced to many countries

robert-le-diable.name: Comma butterfly
descriptions: Ragged wing edges look like a dead leaf when closed
Small white comma mark on underwing gives its English name
Range has expanded northward with climate change
Caterpillar feeds on nettles, hops, and elms
One of the first butterflies seen in spring

gaze.name: Black-veined white
descriptions: Wings are translucent, almost transparent
Delicate appearance gives it an ethereal quality
Has declined in the British Isles due to habitat loss
Caterpillars feed on hawthorn and blackthorn
Found in meadows and orchards across Europe and Asia

fourmi-legionnaire.name: Army ant
descriptions: Does not build a permanent nest; it is always on the move
Colony of up to 700,000 forms a living bivouac from bodies
Raids overwhelm prey through sheer numbers
Has powerful mandibles relative to its body size
Found in the tropical forests of the Americas and Africa

guepe-commune.name: Common wasp
descriptions: Can sting multiple times unlike honey bees
Builds papery nests from chewed wood pulp
Important predator of garden pest insects
Attracted to sugary foods and drinks in late summer
Colony dies off in winter; only queens survive

phasme-geant.name: Chinese giant stick insect
descriptions: Can grow over 50 cm long including legs
One of the longest insects in the world
Mimics a large stick or branch perfectly
Found in tropical forests of Southeast Asia and Australia
Can regenerate lost limbs after molting

cercope-sanguin.name: Red-and-black froghopper
descriptions: Bright red and black coloring warns of bad taste
Nymphs hide inside blobs of protective froth on plants
The froth is called cuckoo spit
Feeds on plant sap through piercing mouthparts
Found in meadows and hedgerows across Europe

chrysope-verte.name: Green lacewing
descriptions: Larvae are voracious predators of aphids
Called aphid lions for their pest-destroying appetite
Adults have delicate lace-like transparent wings
Releases a foul smell when handled
Common beneficial insect in gardens and agriculture

grand-paon-de-nuit.name: Giant peacock moth
descriptions: Largest moth in Europe with a wingspan up to 15 cm
Has four large eyespots to scare off predators
Adults do not eat; they live only to reproduce
Males detect female pheromones from several km away
Found in warm regions of southern Europe

grenouille-verte.name: European green frog
descriptions: Males call loudly at night from ponds and wetlands
Found across most of Europe in freshwater habitats
Can jump up to 20 times its own body length
Breathes through its skin as well as its lungs
Hibernates at the bottom of ponds in winter

grenouille-rousse.name: Common frog
descriptions: One of the most common frogs in Europe
Spawns in huge masses of frogspawn in early spring
Can survive freezing temperatures by producing antifreeze
Dark mask behind the eye is a key identification feature
Males call from underwater during breeding season

grenouille-taureau.name: American bullfrog
descriptions: Largest frog in North America at up to 20 cm
Deep bellowing call sounds like a bull's roar
Will eat almost anything it can fit in its mouth
Highly invasive species outside North America
Can leap up to 2 meters in a single bound

grenouille-aux-yeux-rouges.name: Red-eyed tree frog
descriptions: Bright red eyes may startle predators when opened suddenly
Vivid green body with blue and yellow striped sides
Found in tropical rainforests of Central America
Sleeps on leaves during the day with eyes closed
Eggs hatch early if they sense snake vibrations

rainette-verte.name: European tree frog
descriptions: Climbs trees using suction-cup-like toe pads
Males inflate vocal sacs to amplify their calls
Bright green skin helps it blend with foliage
Found across Europe in warm humid habitats
Changes color from green to brown based on temperature

dendrobate-fraise.name: Strawberry poison frog
descriptions: Bright red color warns predators of its skin toxins
Carries tadpoles on its back to water-filled bromeliads
Found only in Central American tropical rainforests
Each female deposits one tadpole per bromeliad pool
Returns to feed tadpoles with unfertilized eggs

dendrobate-bleu.name: Blue poison dart frog
descriptions: Brilliant blue color warns of toxic skin secretions
Found only in a small area of southern Suriname
Toxins come from the insects it eats in the wild
Males wrestle each other for territory
Captive-bred individuals lose their toxicity

phyllobate-terrible.name: Golden poison frog
descriptions: Most toxic animal on Earth by skin secretion
One frog has enough poison to kill 10 adult humans
Indigenous people use its toxin on blow darts
Tiny frog, only about 5 cm long
Found only in the rainforests of western Colombia

grenouille-de-verre.name: Glass frog
descriptions: Transparent belly reveals its internal organs
Heart, liver, and intestines are visible from below
Lives in tropical rainforest canopies near streams
Males guard egg clutches on leaves over water
Found in Central and South America

grenouille-goliath.name: Goliath frog
descriptions: Largest frog in the world at up to 32 cm
Can weigh over 3 kg
Has no vocal sac and cannot croak
Found only in Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea
Moves rocks to build nesting pools for its eggs

grenouille-tomate.name: Tomato frog
descriptions: Bright tomato-red color warns of skin toxins
Found only on the island of Madagascar
Puffs up its body to appear larger when threatened
Secretes a glue-like toxic substance from its skin
Lives on the forest floor in leaf litter

grenouille-volante-de-wallace.name: Wallace's flying frog
descriptions: Glides up to 15 meters between trees using webbed feet
Extra-large webbed feet act as parachutes
Named after naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace
Lives in the canopy of Borneo's rainforests
Lands on tree trunks with its oversized toe pads

crapaud-commun.name: Common toad
descriptions: Walks rather than hops, unlike most frogs
Secretes a toxic milky substance from parotid glands
Migrates to ancestral breeding ponds each spring
Can live over 40 years in captivity
Found across Europe in gardens, forests, and wetlands

crapaud-accoucheur.name: Common midwife toad
descriptions: Male wraps strings of eggs around his hind legs
Carries eggs for weeks until they are ready to hatch
Releases tadpoles into water when they are developed
Calls with a high-pitched bell-like tone at night
Also known as the midwife toad

crapaud-du-colorado.name: Colorado river toad
descriptions: Produces powerful toxins including bufotenin
Lives in the Sonoran Desert of the southwestern US
One of the largest toads in North America
Emerges from underground only during monsoon rains
Toxins can be fatal to dogs that mouth them

crapaud-de-surinam.name: Surinam toad
descriptions: Flat body looks like a dead leaf on the river bottom
Eggs develop embedded in the skin of the mother's back
Fully formed baby toads emerge from the mother's skin
Has no tongue and pushes food into its mouth with hands
Found in murky waters of South America

crapaud-dore.name: Golden toad
descriptions: Extinct since 1989, possibly from climate change and disease
Was found only in a small cloud forest in Costa Rica
Males were brilliant orange-gold; females were darker
Symbol of modern amphibian extinction crisis
Disappeared after an unusually warm dry year

salamandre-tachetee.name: Fire salamander
descriptions: Bright yellow and black pattern warns of toxic skin
Can live over 20 years in the wild
Gives birth to live larvae in some mountain populations
Secretes toxins strong enough to irritate human skin
Found in damp forests across Europe

axolotl.name: Axolotl
descriptions: Can regenerate limbs, organs, and even parts of its brain
Never undergoes metamorphosis; stays aquatic for life
Found only in Lake Xochimilco near Mexico City
Critically endangered in the wild
Name means 'water monster' in the Aztec language

triton-crete.name: Northern crested newt
descriptions: Males grow a tall jagged crest during breeding
One of the largest newts in Europe at 16 cm
Belly is bright orange with black spots for warning
Lives in ponds in spring and on land the rest of the year
Declining across Europe due to pond loss

triton-palme.name: Palmate newt
descriptions: Males develop webbed hind feet during breeding season
Smallest newt species in Europe at about 9 cm
Tail ends in a thin filament in breeding males
Found in ponds, ditches, and puddles across Europe
More tolerant of acidic water than other newts

salamandre-geante-de-chine.name: Chinese giant salamander
descriptions: Largest amphibian in the world at up to 1.8 meters
Can live over 50 years in the wild
Breathes mainly through its wrinkled skin
Critically endangered due to hunting and habitat loss
Has barely changed in 170 million years

salamandre-geante-du-japon.name: Japanese giant salamander
descriptions: Second largest amphibian, up to 1.5 meters long
Lives in fast-flowing mountain streams
Males guard nests in underwater dens for months
Called a living fossil for its ancient lineage
Protected as a national treasure in Japan

protee-anguillard.name: Olm
descriptions: Blind cave salamander that lives in total darkness
Has no eyes and no skin pigment as an adult
Can survive without food for up to 10 years
Lives in underground caves of the Balkans
Also called the human fish for its pink skin color

triton-alpestre.name: Alpine newt
descriptions: Males turn vivid blue with orange belly in breeding season
One of the most colorful amphibians in Europe
Found in mountain areas up to 2,500 meters altitude
Can survive being frozen in ice temporarily
Lives in ponds during spring and in forests the rest of year

cecilie-de-thompson.name: Thompson's caecilian
descriptions: Legless amphibian that looks like a large earthworm
Burrows underground using its hardened skull
Has tentacles near its eyes for chemical sensing
Found in tropical regions of Central and South America
Mothers feed their skin to their young

cecilie-aquatique.name: Aquatic caecilian
descriptions: One of few fully aquatic caecilian species
Snake-like body with no legs, eyes barely visible
Found in rivers and streams of South America
Can grow up to 60 cm long
Hunts worms and small fish by detecting vibrations

sonneur-a-ventre-jaune.name: Yellow-bellied toad
descriptions: Flashes its bright yellow belly to warn of toxic skin
Arches its back to display warning colors when threatened
Lives in shallow muddy pools and puddles
Heart-shaped pupils are unique among European frogs
Found across central and southern Europe

xenope-lisse.name: African clawed frog
descriptions: First animal ever cloned in a laboratory in 1958
Has claws on three toes, unusual for a frog
Entirely aquatic and never leaves the water
Used in early human pregnancy tests
Lateral line system detects water vibrations like fish

euprocte-des-pyrenees.name: Pyrenean brook salamander
descriptions: Found only in the Pyrenees mountains of France and Spain
Lives in cold mountain streams above 1,000 meters
Breathes mainly through its skin in oxygen-rich water
One of the rarest amphibians in Europe
Males have a bony spur on their tail for mating

crabe-royal-du-kamtchatka.name: Red king crab
descriptions: Leg span can reach up to 1.8 meters
Not a true crab; more closely related to hermit crabs
One of the most commercially valuable crustaceans
Lives in cold waters of the North Pacific
Can weigh up to 12 kg

crabe-araignee-geant-du-japon.name: Japanese spider crab
descriptions: Largest living arthropod with leg span up to 3.8 meters
Lives at depths of 150 to 600 meters off Japan
Can live up to 100 years
Moves slowly on the deep sea floor scavenging for food
Shell is covered in barnacles and sponges for camouflage

tourteau.name: Edible crab
descriptions: Most commercially important crab in Europe
Can weigh up to 3 kg with a shell 25 cm wide
Has a pie-crust edge pattern on its shell
Powerful claws can crush shellfish and sea urchins
Migrates seasonally along the coast

crabe-bleu.name: Blue crab
descriptions: Males have bright blue claws and olive shell
Important food species along the US Atlantic coast
Can swim using flattened paddle-shaped back legs
Females mate only once but store sperm for life
Named for the blue color of its claws

crabe-violoniste.name: Fiddler crab
descriptions: Males have one enormously oversized claw
Waves its giant claw to attract females
The large claw can be 50 percent of its body weight
Lives in mudflats and mangrove swamps
If the big claw is lost, the other grows to replace it

crabe-des-cocotiers.name: Coconut crab
descriptions: Largest terrestrial arthropod, up to 4 kg
Can crack open coconuts with its powerful claws
Climbs palm trees to reach coconuts and fruit
Cannot swim as an adult despite being a crustacean
Has an excellent sense of smell

bernard-l-hermite.name: Hermit crab
descriptions: Uses empty snail shells to protect its soft abdomen
Lines up by size to exchange shells in a chain
Must find a larger shell as it grows
Some species live on land, others in the ocean
Popular as aquarium and terrarium pets

crabe-fer-a-cheval.name: Horseshoe crab
descriptions: Not a true crab; closer to spiders and scorpions
Has existed for over 450 million years, a living fossil
Blue blood is used to test medical products for safety
Has 10 eyes of various types
Comes ashore in huge numbers to spawn on beaches

homard-europeen.name: European lobster
descriptions: Dark blue color turns red only when cooked
Can live over 60 years in the wild
Claws are different: one crushes, the other cuts
Grows by molting its entire exoskeleton
Found on rocky sea floors of the northeast Atlantic

homard-americain.name: American lobster
descriptions: Can weigh over 20 kg, the largest ever was 20.1 kg
Claws are so strong they can crush a tin can
Was once considered food for the poor in colonial America
Lives in the cold Atlantic waters of North America
Lobsters continue to grow throughout their lives

langouste-rouge.name: European spiny lobster
descriptions: Has no claws, unlike lobsters
Uses long antennae to detect predators and food
Can make a loud screeching sound by rubbing antennae
Migrates in single-file lines along the ocean floor
Highly prized as a seafood delicacy

langoustine.name: Norway lobster
descriptions: Also called Norway lobster or scampi
Lives in burrows on muddy sea floors
Emerges from its burrow mainly at night to feed
Claws are long and slender compared to true lobsters
One of the most valuable shellfish in Europe

crevette-rose.name: Common prawn
descriptions: Actually grey when alive; turns pink only when cooked
Lives in large schools in the Atlantic Ocean
Important food source for fish, whales, and seabirds
Has a transparent body when young
Can swim both forward and backward by flipping its tail

crevette-mante-paon.name: Peacock mantis shrimp
descriptions: Punches prey with the speed of a bullet at 83 km/h
Strike generates heat and light through cavitation
Can see 16 types of color including ultraviolet
Punch force can break aquarium glass
Most complex visual system in the animal kingdom

crevette-nettoyeuse.name: Pacific cleaner shrimp
descriptions: Sets up cleaning stations on coral reefs
Removes parasites from fish that visit its station
Waves its white antennae to advertise its services
Even large predatory fish wait patiently to be cleaned
Found on coral reefs throughout the tropics

crevette-pistolet.name: Pistol shrimp
descriptions: Snaps its claw to create a shockwave louder than a gunshot
Sound reaches 218 decibels, one of the loudest in nature
Shockwave stuns or kills small prey
Snap creates a brief flash of light and heat
Lives in burrows on tropical sea floors

crevette-grise.name: Brown shrimp
descriptions: Common small shrimp of European shallow coastal waters
Lives half-buried in sand on the sea floor
Important food source for many fish and seabirds
Harvested by traditional shrimp trawlers in the North Sea
Transparent body provides camouflage over sandy bottoms

krill-antarctique.name: Antarctic krill
descriptions: One of the most abundant animal species on Earth
Total biomass estimated at over 500 million tonnes
Keystone species feeding whales, seals, and penguins
Swarms can be visible from space
Lives up to 6 years in Antarctic waters

ecrevisse-a-pattes-blanches.name: White-clawed crayfish
descriptions: Native freshwater crayfish of Europe
Named for its pale white underside of the claws
Indicator of clean unpolluted streams
Declining due to disease spread by invasive crayfish
Can live up to 10 years in the right habitat

cloporte-commun.name: Common woodlouse
descriptions: Only crustacean fully adapted to life on land
Rolls into a ball when threatened, called a pill bug
Breathes through modified gills that must stay moist
Eats decaying plant matter, recycling nutrients
Mother carries eggs in a fluid-filled pouch

balane-commune.name: Common acorn barnacle
descriptions: Cements itself headfirst permanently to hard surfaces
Feeds by kicking food into its mouth with its legs
Has the strongest natural glue known to science
Related to crabs and shrimps despite looking like a shell
Charles Darwin spent 8 years studying barnacles

daphnie.name: Water flea
descriptions: Known as the water flea for its jerky swimming
Transparent body lets you see its beating heart
Can reproduce without mating through parthenogenesis
Widely used as a model organism in science labs
Important food source for freshwater fish

anatife.name: Goose barnacle
descriptions: Attaches to floating objects like driftwood and ships
People once believed barnacle geese hatched from them
Has a long flexible stalk and feathery feeding legs
Filter feeds on plankton from ocean currents
Found in oceans worldwide on floating debris

galathee.name: Squat lobster
descriptions: Also called the squat lobster for its flattened body
Tucks its tail under its body like a crab
Found on rocky shores and in deep-sea habitats
Can flick its tail rapidly to escape backward
Closely related to hermit crabs, not true lobsters

araignee-de-mer.name: European spider crab
descriptions: Has a spiny shell covered in algae for camouflage
Migrates in large groups along the sea floor
Important commercial crab species in Europe
Can grow to a shell width of over 20 cm
Uses its long legs to walk slowly across the seabed

pieuvre-commune.name: Common octopus
descriptions: Has three hearts and blue blood
Can change color and texture in milliseconds
Squeezes through any gap larger than its beak
Has been observed using coconut shells as shelter
Each arm has a mind of its own with its own neurons

pieuvre-a-anneaux-bleus.name: Blue-ringed octopus
descriptions: Small enough to fit in your palm but deadly venomous
Venom can kill a human in minutes with no antidote
Blue rings flash brightly as a warning before biting
Found in tide pools of the Pacific and Indian Oceans
One of the most venomous animals in the world

pieuvre-mimetique.name: Mimic octopus
descriptions: Can impersonate over 15 different species
Mimics lionfish, flatfish, and sea snakes
Changes shape, color, and behavior to match its model
Found on sandy bottoms of the Indo-Pacific
Discovered by scientists only in 1998

calmar-geant.name: Giant squid
descriptions: Has the largest eyes in the animal kingdom at 27 cm
Lives in the deep ocean and is rarely seen alive
Can grow up to 13 meters long including tentacles
Inspired legends of the Kraken sea monster
Was first photographed alive in its habitat in 2004

calmar-colossal.name: Colossal squid
descriptions: Largest invertebrate by weight at up to 500 kg
Has rotating hooks on its tentacles for gripping prey
Lives in the deep Antarctic Ocean
Eyes are the largest of any animal at 27 cm across
Main prey of the sperm whale in deep waters

seiche-commune.name: Common cuttlefish
descriptions: Can change color faster than a chameleon
Has W-shaped pupils for excellent vision
Cuttlebone helps control its buoyancy underwater
Shoots ink as a decoy to escape predators
Has three hearts, like its octopus relatives

nautile.name: Chambered nautilus
descriptions: Living fossil that has survived over 500 million years
Has up to 90 tentacles but no suckers
Shell is divided into gas-filled chambers for buoyancy
Lives in the deep tropical Pacific and Indian Oceans
Inspired the spiral design in mathematics and art

calmar-de-humboldt.name: Humboldt squid
descriptions: Aggressive predator nicknamed the red devil
Can change between red and white in rapid flashes
Hunts in packs of up to 1,200 individuals
Found in the deep waters of the eastern Pacific
Can grow up to 1.8 meters and weigh 50 kg

escargot-de-bourgogne.name: Burgundy snail
descriptions: The classic French escargot served in garlic butter
Can seal itself in its shell with a mucus lid for winter
Has both male and female reproductive organs
Shell can reach 5 cm in diameter
Found in vineyards and gardens across Europe

escargot-petit-gris.name: Garden snail
descriptions: One of the most commonly eaten snails in Europe
Smaller than the Burgundy snail at about 3 cm
Can aestivate in dry weather by sealing its shell
Active mainly at night and after rain
Leaves a slime trail that other snails can follow

limace-rouge.name: Large red slug
descriptions: Can be red, orange, brown, or even black
Important decomposer that recycles dead plant material
Produces thick sticky mucus for protection and movement
Has a breathing hole on its right side called a pneumostome
Can stretch to several times its contracted length

nudibranche-espagnol.name: Spanish dancer
descriptions: Bright red and yellow coloring warns of toxic taste
One of the largest nudibranchs in the Mediterranean
Gets its toxins from the sponges it eats
Has feathery gills on its back for breathing
Also called the Spanish dancer for its swimming motion

cone-geographe.name: Geography cone
descriptions: One of the most venomous snails in the world
Harpoon-like tooth injects rapid-acting venom
Venom contains compounds being studied for painkillers
Can be fatal to humans if handled carelessly
Found in tropical Indo-Pacific coral reefs

ormeau.name: Abalone
descriptions: Prized as a luxury seafood especially in East Asia
Inner shell has an iridescent mother-of-pearl layer
Clings to rocks with an incredibly strong muscular foot
Breathes through a row of holes along its shell
Some species are farmed commercially

patelle.name: Common limpet
descriptions: Clings to rocks with a suction force of 75 kg per sq cm
Returns to the exact same spot on its home rock
Scrapes algae from rocks with a tongue harder than iron
Conical shell is one of the strongest shapes in nature
Found on rocky shores worldwide

moule-commune.name: Blue mussel
descriptions: Attaches to rocks using incredibly strong byssus threads
Filters up to 65 liters of water per day
Forms dense beds that create habitat for other species
One of the most widely farmed shellfish in the world
Byssus glue is studied for waterproof adhesive development

huitre-plate.name: European flat oyster
descriptions: Has been eaten by humans for thousands of years
Changes sex during its lifetime, alternating each season
Filters up to 200 liters of water per day
Beds create crucial reef habitat in coastal waters
Pearl formation occurs when an irritant enters the shell

coquille-saint-jacques.name: Great scallop
descriptions: Has up to 200 tiny blue eyes along the edge of its shell
Can swim by clapping its shells together
Shell is the symbol of the pilgrimage to Santiago
Highly prized as a gourmet seafood
Eyes have mirror-like reflectors similar to a telescope

palourde.name: Carpet shell clam
descriptions: Burrows into sand using a muscular foot
Filters plankton and algae from surrounding water
Growth rings on its shell indicate its age
Found in sandy and muddy coastal habitats worldwide
An important species in aquaculture and fisheries

tridacne-geant.name: Giant clam
descriptions: Largest living bivalve, weighing up to 200 kg
Shell can grow over 1.2 meters across
Gets energy from algae living inside its colorful mantle
Once it settles, it never moves again
Found on coral reefs of the Indo-Pacific

moule-d-eau-douce.name: Freshwater pearl mussel
descriptions: Can live over 100 years, one of the longest-lived animals
Filters river water, improving water quality
Larvae are parasites that attach to fish gills
Declining worldwide due to pollution and habitat loss
Once used to produce freshwater pearls

couteau.name: Razor clam
descriptions: Shell shaped like a straight razor or knife handle
Burrows into sand at remarkable speed using its foot
Can withdraw deep into sand to avoid predators
Prized as a seafood delicacy in Europe and Asia
Two siphons extend to filter water while buried

praire.name: Warty venus
descriptions: Long-lived bivalve that can live over 50 years
Growth rings on its thick shell record its age
Prized clam in French gastronomy
Burrows just below the surface in sandy sea floors
Found along the Atlantic coast of Europe

coque.name: Common cockle
descriptions: Heart-shaped shell when viewed from the side
Burrows just below the sand surface in intertidal zones
Uses its muscular foot to leap and escape predators
Important food species harvested by hand on tidal flats
Found on sandy beaches across Europe

mygale-de-leblond.name: Goliath birdeater
descriptions: Largest spider in the world by mass at over 170 g
Leg span can reach 30 cm across
Can flick urticating hairs at predators from its abdomen
Found in the rainforests of South America
Despite its name, rarely eats birds

mygale-a-genoux-rouges.name: Mexican redknee tarantula
descriptions: Named for the bright red-orange patches on its legs
One of the most popular pet tarantulas worldwide
