Docile temperament makes it suitable for beginners
Native to the dry scrubland of Mexico
Can live up to 30 years in captivity as a female

veuve-noire.name: Black widow
descriptions: Venom is 15 times stronger than a rattlesnake's
Females sometimes eat males after mating
Red hourglass marking on abdomen is a warning sign
Builds messy irregular webs in sheltered spots
Found across temperate and tropical regions worldwide

araignee-des-jardins.name: European garden spider
descriptions: Builds beautiful orb webs up to 60 cm across
Rebuilds its web every day eating the old silk first
Wraps prey in silk faster than the eye can follow
Common in gardens and hedgerows across Europe
Harmless to humans despite its large size

argiope-frelon.name: Wasp spider
descriptions: Bold yellow and black stripes mimic a wasp
Weaves a distinctive zigzag pattern in its web
Zigzag called a stabilimentum may attract insects
Found in sunny meadows and gardens across Europe
Female is five times larger than the male

araignee-sauteuse.name: Jumping spider
descriptions: Has the best vision of any spider with large front eyes
Pounces on prey from several body lengths away
Does not build a web to catch prey
Over 6,000 species make it the largest spider family
Can see in color and perceives UV light

araignee-loup.name: Wolf spider
descriptions: Hunts prey by chasing it down on the ground
Mother carries her egg sac attached to her spinnerets
Baby spiders ride on their mother's back after hatching
Has excellent night vision with reflective eyes
Found worldwide in grasslands and forests

araignee-errante-du-bresil.name: Brazilian wandering spider
descriptions: One of the most venomous spiders in the world
Wanders the forest floor at night hunting prey
Does not build a web; hunts actively on the ground
Sometimes found hiding in banana shipments
Venom contains a compound studied for medical uses

araignee-a-toile-d-entonnoir.name: Sydney funnel-web spider
descriptions: Builds a funnel-shaped web and waits at the narrow end
Sydney funnel-web is one of the deadliest spiders
Can strike and bite in a fraction of a second
Fangs are strong enough to pierce a fingernail
An antivenom exists and no deaths since its introduction

nephile-doree.name: Golden silk orb-weaver
descriptions: Builds the largest webs of any spider, up to 2 meters
Silk has a golden yellow sheen in sunlight
Web silk is stronger than Kevlar by weight
Female is up to 10 times larger than the male
Found in tropical regions worldwide

recluse-brune.name: Brown recluse
descriptions: Has a violin-shaped mark on its back
Bite can cause necrosis of the skin tissue
Shy and reclusive, biting only when pressed against skin
Found in central and southern United States
Builds irregular webs in dark undisturbed places

scorpion-empereur.name: Emperor scorpion
descriptions: One of the largest scorpions in the world at 20 cm
Mild venom; sting is no worse than a bee sting
Glows under ultraviolet light due to chemicals in its exoskeleton
Mother carries her babies on her back for weeks
Found in the rainforests of West Africa

scorpion-jaune.name: Deathstalker
descriptions: One of the most dangerous scorpions in the world
Also called the deathstalker scorpion
Venom contains compounds studied for cancer treatment
Found in deserts of North Africa and the Middle East
Small size but extremely potent neurotoxic venom

scorpion-d-arizona.name: Arizona bark scorpion
descriptions: Most venomous scorpion in North America
Can climb walls and ceilings inside homes
Glows bright green under ultraviolet light
Sting causes intense pain and numbness
Found in the Sonoran Desert of the southwestern US

scorpion-noir-a-queue-epaisse.name: Black fat-tailed scorpion
descriptions: Thick powerful tail delivers a very painful sting
One of the most dangerous scorpions in southern Africa
Dark coloring provides camouflage at night
Can go months without food or water
Neurotoxic venom can be life-threatening to humans

tique-du-mouton.name: Sheep tick
descriptions: Feeds on blood of mammals, including humans
Can transmit Lyme disease and other illnesses
Waits on vegetation with front legs outstretched
Can survive over a year without feeding
Swells to many times its body size when engorged

acarien-rouge.name: Red spider mite
descriptions: Tiny red mite often seen running on walls in summer
Most species are harmless plant feeders
Some species are serious agricultural pests
Barely visible to the naked eye at under 1 mm
Found in gardens and on plants worldwide

sarcopte-de-la-gale.name: Scabies mite
descriptions: Microscopic mite that burrows into human skin
Causes intense itching from an allergic reaction
Female tunnels into skin to lay eggs
Has affected humans for over 2,500 years
Spreads through prolonged skin-to-skin contact

solifuge.name: Camel spider
descriptions: Neither a spider nor a scorpion, but a separate order
Has the largest jaws relative to body of any arachnid
Can run at speeds up to 16 km/h
Found in deserts worldwide, also called camel spiders
Non-venomous despite fearsome appearance

faucheux.name: Harvestman
descriptions: Not a true spider; belongs to a separate arachnid order
Has only one body segment, unlike spiders' two
Cannot produce silk or venom
Legs continue to twitch after detached to distract predators
Also known as the harvestman or daddy longlegs

python-reticule.name: Reticulated python
descriptions: Longest snake in the world, recorded over 8 meters
Complex geometric pattern provides excellent camouflage
Found in Southeast Asian forests and near water
Excellent swimmer and has colonized many islands
Can eat prey as large as a deer

lezard-ocelle.name: Ocellated lizard
descriptions: Largest lizard in Europe at up to 60 cm
Striking blue eyespots along its flanks
Found in Mediterranean scrubland and dry forests
Can deliver a painful bite if handled
Feeds on insects, small mammals, and fruit
